📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Freddie Cotton | 20 Nov 2026 21:07, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:15.

Marseille welcome Le Mans to the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening for round 11 of the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign.

In their previous league outing, Les Olympiens claimed a commendable 2-1 victory over Lens at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis, while Les Manceaux scored late against Monaco on home soil to salvage a point.

Following a dismal start to the current league campaign, losing five of their opening six matches to leave them languishing inside the relegation zone and just one point off the foot of the table at the end of September, Marseille will be delighted with how they have bounced back in recent weeks.

Since their narrow 2-1 loss to back-to-back European champions Paris Saint-Germain on September 20, Les Olympiens have been an unstoppable force, winning each of their previous five domestic matches to rise to fourth in the Ligue 1 table and sit just five points off Les Parisiens at the summit.

The biggest strength of Bruno Genesio’s side has undoubtedly been their free flowing attack, as after 10 league games, Marseille have netted an impressive 22 goals, a tally that cannot be bettered by any other side in the division.

However, Les Olympiens will undoubtedly be disappointed with their performances in the UEFA Europa League, as after four league phase fixtures they have picked up just three points and presently reside outside of the tournament’s progression places to the knockout stage.

Having gone unbeaten in each of their previous six encounters with Le Mans, including a 2-1 victory in their most recent meeting at the Stade Velodrome in January 2010, Marseille will be confident that they can continue their fine league form this weekend though and mount a charge towards PSG in top spot.

It has been revealed that after ending their 16-year wait for promotion to France’s top tier at the end of the 2025-26 campaign, beating Bastia 2-0 away from home on the final day to pip St. Etienne to second place, Le Mans will have mixed feelings about their start to life in Ligue 1 this season.

Although they lost just one of their opening five Ligue 1 matches to start the campaign, Patrick Videira’s men have failed to claim a league victory in over two months, leaving them 15th in the table with eight points and only outside of the relegation places on goal difference.

Without a doubt, Les Manceaux’s weakness in the 2026-27 season has been their leaky defence, as Sunday’s visitors have conceded a concerning 19 league goals so far and are one of three sides alongside Lens and Strasbourg that are yet to keep a clean sheet.

Despite previously claiming victory at the Stade Velodrome, posting a famous 3-2 win in September 1994, Le Mans head into Sunday’s match in poor form, facing Marseille as massive underdogs, and knowing they’ll need to pull off another monumental triumph if they want to get their season back on track this weekend.

Marseille form (all competitions):.

Le Mans form (all competitions):.

Marseille are still without Italian full-back Emerson Palmieri, who is expected to return before the end of the year from a knee glitch, while Canadian midfielder Derek Cornelius continues his struggles with a hip problem.

On a more positive note, Genesio will be glad that a cohort of notable first team players including the likes of Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Nayef Aguerd and Geoffrey Kondogbia have all returned from the international break unscathed.

Netting an impressive seven Ligue 1 goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous three league outings, Amine Gouiri is undoubtedly Les Olympiens’ dangerman and will be hoping to close the gap to Paris FC’s Lassine Sinayoko at the top of the division’s scoring charts on Sunday evening.

Le Mans are certain to be missing Algerian midfielder Adil Bourabaa and former Everton defender Djibril Sidibe this weekend as the pair are ruled out with ankle and foot injuries respectively.

It remains to be seen whether either Samuel Yohou, who has reportedly sustained a head injury, or young French midfielder Martin Rossignol can fight off complications to feature at the Stade Velodrome too.

After signing from Ligue 2 side Guingamp in the summer, 32-year-old striker Louis Mafouta has been the visitors’ biggest attacking threat this season, scoring a respectable four goals in 10 league matches.

Marseille possible starting lineup:.

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Hojbjerg, Nnadi; Harit, Abdelli, Paixao; Gouiri.

Le Mans possible starting lineup:.

Kocik; Bamba, Torrente, Voyer; Vercruysse; Buades, Traore, Bretelle, Calodat; Mafouta, Gueye.

Having emphatically bounced back from their early season woes, Marseille will be confident that they can beat any opponent they come up against and continue their impressive rise up the table.

Although Le Mans will be desperate to turn around their poor form, we believe the hosts will be far too strong and are backing them to close the gap on the teams above by posting a convincing victory at the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening.

#60830. Upcoming heights and same problems: How Milan stars fared in the November international break

Upcoming heights and same problems: How Milan stars fared in the November international break

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (829 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With just a few days until the return of AC Milan action, the international break is now done.
  • Whether you love it or you hate it, the international break is now over and players are trickling back into Milanello.
  • So, let’s look at what Amorim has returning, with several things to shout about….
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With just a few days until the return of AC Milan action, the international break is now done. Let’s take a look at how the internationals fared.

Whether you love it or you hate it, the international break is now over and players are trickling back into Milanello. Even those who didn’t head away are only just really returning, with Ruben Amorim offering the squad a week off.

So, let’s look at what Amorim has returning, with several things to shout about….

Christian Pulisic probably leaves the break as the star of the week(s). His brace against Haiti helped secure a place in the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, and he then rounded it off with a bicycle kick in the second leg.

After missing the penultimate international break of the season – to ensure he was fully back to fitness – he’s quickly reminded everyone of how vital he can be for club and country, scoring his seventh goal of the season in only 13 games.

He’s on fire and there are no signs of him slowing down anytime soon.

You’d then have to speak about Diego Moreira, who has left the international break – somehow – with more praise than he started it with. He starred in Belgium’s 2-1 win against Turkiye and then followed that up with a goal against Italy.

It gets to a point where you run out of superlatives to describe a player and his teammates are already at that stage. Both Mark Van Bommel and Koni De Winter have called him crazy (in a good way), with the former even putting him in the same group as Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

He’s become a starter for the Red Devils and it’s difficult to see that changing.

Sources indicate that in terms of the Italians, Milan had a few reasons to smile and it starts with Alphadjo Cisse. At first, it seemed he’d been wasted during the break, with Roberto Mancini not calling him up for the game against France.

However, he was given the nod for the second game and got some valuable minutes on the field. As the Rossoneri have become familiar with, he took that chance with both hands, scoring a disallowed goal and winning a penalty in a defeat to Belgium.

He’s shining with confidence right now and long may it continue.

Sources indicate that then, Francesco Camarda is probably at the other end of the scale. He’s clearly not got the most confidence when representing the Diavolo, but returning to the youth level, he shone like he always has.

Against Sankhoun Diawara’s France side, he was excellent. In terms of his hold-up play, finishing and just general performance, he was almost perfect, if not perfect. With a goal to round it off too, he leaves the break with a much-needed confidence boost.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, we can’t say the same for Goncalo Ramos. After Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, this was a chance for him to take the star role and prove that he’s going to be the man to ensure things keep ticking.

Instead, he left the break leaving Portugal with more questions than answers, which is a familiar feeling.

In a recent development, he played just shy of 150 minutes during the break and mustered just one shot. It’s not like he provided an assist or any key passes either. In other words, it’s another blank for him and it’s clearly having an effect.

Without a goal in 661 minutes, it’s no shock why the Diavolo are so heavily pursuing a striker ahead of January.

For France, it was a relatively quiet break for Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot. Neither performed especially well against Italy in a 3-1 loss at San Siro, though Rabiot was named as the captain for that game. Then, in the second game, Maignan was injured. However, it seems he’ll be fine for this weekend.

Not a lot to shout about for those two, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing either.

For Luka Modric, his minutes were focused in the right areas. He played 14 minutes in a nothing game against England, but was then essential in a 2-1 win against the Czech Republic, which may help them qualify for the latter stages of the Nations League.

In a recent development, it was another strange international break for Ardon Jashari, too. He was given no minutes against Slovenia in a 0-0 draw, but then played the full 90 minutes against Scotland, where they won 4-0. He made 76 passes from 90 touches, so he had some involvement. However, he’s still a way away from being a dictator of the team, as it was hoped he’d be.

Davide Bartesaghi, Christian Comotto and Sankhoun Diawara were all given valuable minutes during the break. Finally, Pervis Estupinan played 36 minutes over the break. He returns without any injuries and that’s all there is to really say about his past fortnight.

There was every reason to expect a cracking game – the Barrowmen had won 4–1 at Hastings United the previous weekend in front of more than 1,000 fans, while visitors Punjab United were unbeaten in seven league games.

It has been revealed that the floodlights came on just ten minutes into a cold Saturday afternoon, and a crowd of 125 saw Punjab race into a four-goal lead inside 34 minutes. Steyning pulled two back after the break, but the visitors held on for a 4–2 win.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

According to recent reports, punjab took the lead with the first chance of the game. Emmanuel Oluwasemo picked out Chris Edwards at the back post with a fine delivery, and Edwards headed in off the post.

A couple of minutes later, Edwards turned provider, picking out Roman Campbell, whose bullet header flew past Alfie Mansell to make it 2–0.

Industry observers note that things went from bad to worse for the Barrowmen before the half-hour. Campbell pounced on a mistake by Marcus Allen and squared for Jack Hopkins, who rolled the ball into an empty net for Punjab’s third.

Steyning were forced into a change when Max Blencowe went off injured after a late studs-up tackle. The Punjab defender was shown a yellow card, while some thought the challenge worthy of a red. Bright Kuntu-Blankson came on to replace Blencowe.

A couple of minutes later, Punjab had their fourth. Sam Wood swung in a corner in the 34th minute, and the ball somehow found its way into the net.

The Barrowmen had a couple of half-chances to pull one back before the break.

Sources indicate that with his side four down, boss Brannon O’Neil had a major half-time team talk on his hands. And Town came out with more energy after the break and created several chances, but Punjab held firm.

Midway through the half, Jesse Sentamu came off the bench to score for the second week running, pulling one back with his third goal of the season.

Steyning kept up the pressure and Jared Rance added a second in the 90th minute. But The first-half damage proved too much to undo, and Punjab left the Shooting Field with all three points.

Man of the match: Roman Campbell.

Punjab’s win extended their unbeaten league run to eight matches and lifted them to ninth in the table while the Barrowmen dropped to 15th.

It has been revealed that steyning return to cup action in midweek when they travel to Faversham Town in the third round of the Velocity Cup. Kick-off is at 7.45pm. They visit Margate on Saturday.

Steyning Town: Alfie Mansell, Tad Bromage, Max Blencowe, Harvey Woollard, Marcus Allen, Ryan Worrall, (captain), Alex Brewer, Conrad Michael Honore, Leo Marley Ginger, Adam Adam, Jared Rance.

Sassuolo vs. Genoa - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (638 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 21:13.
  • Roberto D'Aversa's Sassuolo tenure begins against Genoa on Sunday, with the Neroverdi in danger of slipping into the relegation zone.
  • The matchday 12 encounter pits two sides separated by four places in the Serie A table, with the higher-ranked Rossoblu chasing a fifth consecutive victory in this fixture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 21:13.

Roberto D'Aversa's Sassuolo tenure begins against Genoa on Sunday, with the Neroverdi in danger of slipping into the relegation zone.

The matchday 12 encounter pits two sides separated by four places in the Serie A table, with the higher-ranked Rossoblu chasing a fifth consecutive victory in this fixture.

Sassuolo's brief association with Alberto Aquilani lasted just 11 league matches, with the board in Reggio Emilia making another managerial change to arrest the club's poor run of results.

Admittedly, the Black and Greens made a respectable start under the former midfielder, collecting seven points from their opening four games as a three-match unbeaten run followed an opening-day 2-1 defeat at Atalanta BC.

However, mid-September's 2-1 reverse at Monza began a seven-match winless league sequence, and Sassuolo's defensive record under Aquilani made for grim reading.

The Neroverdi conceded a staggering 19 goals across five defeats, losing 4-2 to Frosinone, 2-0 to Como, 6-2 to Lazio, 4-2 to Fiorentina and 3-0 at Roma.

The defeat at the Olimpico proved the final straw for the 17th-placed outfit, who sit just one point clear of the relegation zone and two ahead of 19th-placed Venezia.

That underlines the scale of the task facing D'Aversa, who inherits a side that have conceded 29 Serie A goals, four more than both Monza and bottom-placed Udinese, two of the teams at the moment occupying the relegation places.

Daniele De Rossi's men will hope that the new boss needs time to adapt to his surroundings as they seek to extend the Black and Greens' losing sequence.

The travelling supporters will welcome this weekend's trip, given that the Grifone have claimed four consecutive victories in this fixture, including two at Mapei Stadium.

Beyond those recent successes in Reggio Emilia, the Ligurian outfit enter this weekend as one of the competition's form teams.

Their 2-1 home defeat to AC Milan before the international break ended Genoa's three-match winning streak, during which they stunned Juventus 2-0 in front of their supporters.

Having collected 12 points from their last 18 in Serie A, losing to Roma and Milan during that improved run, De Rossi's men will back themselves to overcome any fresh-manager bounce in Emilia-Romagna and claim consecutive away league victories for the first time since November-December 2024, when they beat Parma 1-0 and Udinese 2-0.

D'Aversa has several fitness concerns ahead of his first Sassuolo match: Cristian Volpato, Yeferson Paz, Daniel Boloca, Domenico Berardi and Vasilije Adzic will be assessed before Sunday's clash; however, Fedde Leysen (knee) and Ismael Kone (broken leg) are sidelined.

If three-goal Adzic cannot feature, the fresh manager will have to rely on Sebastiano Esposito and Armand Lauriente, who have scored twice apiece, to shoulder more of the Black and Greens' attacking burden.

Genoa, meanwhile, will look to Milutin Osmajic and Junior Messias to add to their respective Serie A tallies of four and two goals, while Stephan El Shaarawy has registered two assists in his last three appearances for the Ligurian outfit.

A relatively healthy squad further boosts the visitors' prospects, although Morten Frendrup remains doubtful due to the ankle problem that kept him out of the Rossoblu's defeat to Milan last time out.

Sassuolo possible starting lineup:.

Muric; Walukiewicz, Caleta-Car, Idzes, Doig; Thorstvedt, Matic, Sulemana; Dominguez, Lauriente; Esposito.

Genoa possible starting lineup:.

Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Wiafe, Traore, Ellertsson; Junior Messias, El Shaarawy; Osmajic.

Sassuolo's injury doubts complicate D'Aversa's first assignment, particularly with Berardi and Adzic potentially unavailable to bolster an attack already struggling to compensate for the team's defensive frailties.

Genoa arrive with fewer fitness concerns and a confident Osmajic, suggesting that De Rossi's men can secure a fifth successive victory over the Neroverdi.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal have played six Premier League games this season and Bruno Guimarães has been a match-winning force in two of them.
  • According to recent reports, the Brazilian was not signed to be Arsenal’s super sub but that is the role he appears to be playing in these early days in north London.
  • Liquid football from Arsenal 😮‍💨 Bruno Guimarães finishes off a well-worked team move!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have played six Premier League games this season and Bruno Guimarães has been a match-winning force in two of them. At this rate, he might justify his enormous £75m transfer fee by Christmas.

According to recent reports, the Brazilian was not signed to be Arsenal’s super sub but that is the role he appears to be playing in these early days in north London. Against Leeds United here, as it was against Sunderland last month, he came off the bench when the champions were struggling. And as it was at Sunderland, he produced a thumping finish to put Arsenal on their way to three points.

Liquid football from Arsenal 😮‍💨 Bruno Guimarães finishes off a well-worked team move! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/fbLJiaZbX5.

This is the value of signing a 28-year-old with significant Premier League experience. As Arsenal laboured against an impressively organised and courageous Leeds side, Mikel Arteta knew that Guimarães was capable of coming into the game and adjusting to its demands. There has been no adaptation period required for Guimarães, who is fast becoming one of the most popular players in north London.

According to recent reports, the finish, which put Arsenal 2-1 ahead at the Emirates Stadium, marked an emphatic conclusion to a fabulous passing sequence. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice all combined at speed before Guimarães charged on to Rice’s flick. “It was a beauty,” noted Arteta of the goal. The move had actually begun at the feet of Guimarães a few moments earlier, when he nutmegged an opponent in style.

It has been revealed that the winning goal came just eight minutes after Riccardo Calafiori, Arsenal’s thrilling left-back/centre-forward hybrid, had pulled them level in the game. James Justin had struck for Leeds shortly after half-time, creating a horrible anxiety among the home fans here, and for much of the afternoon Daniel Farke’s side were the better team.

Leeds finally have their opener! 🤩 James Justin arrives at the back post to fire them ahead. 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ITjUMSlrG1.

Leeds, though, could not compete with Arsenal for depth. The arrival of Guimarães as a 63rd-minute substitute represented a flexing of Arteta’s managerial muscle, in his first match since signing a new long-term contract, and the Brazilian offered a moment of attacking quality that his opponents were unable to replicate.

Recent findings suggest that it was actually the first competitive home game that Guimarães had played for Arsenal since his transfer from Newcastle United, as a result of a few niggles and the club’s unusual run of four consecutive away matches before the international break. The most recent of those was the 3-0 thrashing by Brighton, which was one of their worst defeats of the last few seasons.

Industry observers note that this gritty victory represented a necessary response to that defeat, even if the performance was far from dominant. “We had a point to prove,” said Arteta. “Something was touched in our identity against Brighton.”.

Industry observers note that guimarães, too, clearly felt that some wrongs needed to be made right. For all his brilliance in this game and against Sunderland, he had produced a horrible showing at the Amex Stadium a few weeks ago. “He was not at that level against Brighton,” noted Arteta. “This is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action you have to be at that level. At Brighton, he wasn’t. Today, he was much better.”.

Leeds had not lost in their opening five Premier League matches of this season and it was easy to see why. They were willing to press Arsenal high up the pitch, taking risks and engaging in physical duels, and the strategy proved hugely effective for an hour.

If they had been more precise in the final third, they could have been a few goals ahead by the time Justin converted Gabriel Gudmundsson’s left-wing cross after 55 minutes. Anton Stach, who was accidentally blocked by team-mate Jayden Bogle, and Gudmundsson both went close in the first half.

David Raya at his very best to deny Leeds the opener 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/hOB8RMapxw.

Industry observers note that “I am heartbroken and gutted for my players,” remarked Farke. “They deserved to travel back with points today. The defeat has to do with the quality of the players they [Arsenal] could bring in. It is down to the mentality Mikel has created here that even on a tough day they find a way to win the game.”.

According to recent reports, right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Sources indicate that arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jim Goodwin was full of pride after watching Dundee United make history with a landmark 4-0 demolition of Hibs.

The visitors recorded their biggest ever win at Easter Road, with Zac Sapsford’s first-half double paving the way for a stunning victory before Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall piled on the misery.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It was a humbling afternoon for Hibs, who thought they had turned a corner under new head coach Marink Reedijk, and the home support deserted the stadium long before the full-time whistle.

Goodwin has experienced some low moments in Leith, losing his job as Aberdeen boss following a 6-0 thrashing to Hibs in January 2023, so was naturally delighted by the margin of this win.

He said: “It’s not been a venue that’s been all too kind to me over the years, so on a personal note I’m very pleased. But, of course, it’s all about Dundee United. I wasn’t aware of that stat but it is something that we can be proud of.

“It’s very rare that you come to a venue like Easter Road against good opposition, especially off the back of their recent results, and have the kind of convincing victory that we’ve just experienced.

According to recent reports, “We scored four good goals. Even the build-up for the first, the penalty, was good.”.

Sapsford got United off the mark after eight minutes, recovering from having his spot-kick saved by Rafa Sallinger to slot home the rebound after Jason Kerr had fouled him.

The Australian doubled his tally six minutes before half-time, guiding Kevin Ciubotaru’s cross into the net at the near post.

United maintained their momentum after the break, with Cameron firing home off the underside of the bar after Daniel Bennie’s effort had struck the post.

Randall completed the rout, lashing a left-footed shot past Sallinger from 15 yards after being teed up by Tait.

Meanwhile, Hibs head coach Reedijk was left struggling to explain Hibs’ sorry collapse after his side had beaten Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final and thumped Aberdeen 4-0 before the international break.

The Dutchman said: “What has happened in these two weeks? I haven’t seen these glimpses that it would happen during the week, if you know what I mean.

It has been revealed that “And it is not that we didn’t create chances or whatever, it is more this basic behaviour which brings you into matches and continues spells and makes the opponent doubt. We had too many of these moments that didn’t fall our way.

“That is something we need to be very sharp with because we know how nice it is to win, but we also now experience how nice it is not to win and especially in this way. I hate losing but in this way I really hate losing.”.

AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic has admitted that he was a fan of Sergio Conceicao, even if his management was rather totalitarian.

Sources indicate that it’s fair to say that Conceicao is a divisive figure within the Milan sphere. The Portuguese arrived and won the Supercoppa Italiana and there were glimpses of the Rossoneri becoming a team under him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that however, there were far too many incidents which turned most against him – including some members of the squad – and that gave him little hope of continuing. So, when he lost the Coppa Italia against Bologna, he was all but done, if he wasn’t before then.

He’s called it unfair since, but logically there was no way he could’ve continued.

Speaking to the Serbian podcast SS Calcio, Pavlovic admitted that he was fond of Conceicao, despite some of his strange methods, as MilanNews relays.

In a recent development, “Conceicao banned Nutella, and since then they haven’t allowed it [he laughs]. He was… He’s a good guy, I like him, but he had Hitler-like methods. We go away for a match and at the hotel we split up; the players stay together, everyone else stays outside.

“Knee and elbow pads are mandatory in training, whether the temperatures are below zero or 35 degrees; they have to be there.

“Three days before a match, some players went to a concert until 11 p.m.… He had assistants, or spies if you like, who reported to him, and he made such a circus out of it that in the next match, none of those five or six players were allowed on the pitch.”.

Another anecdote about Conceiçao, when he had just been appointed coach of Milan….

“He was 40 minutes late to the first meeting; all the players and management were waiting for him, and he was in his office. He just wanted everyone to know who was in charge. He did it on purpose.”.

It’s certainly a strong comparison to make; that’s for sure….

💡 Key Takeaways

  • St Mirren manager Craig McLeish claims self-interest and poor governance are killing Scottish football’s hopes of improvement.
  • McLeish is frustrated that Scottish Football Association chief football officer Craig Mulholland has reportedly had to dilute prepares for young player quotas to appease five William Hill Premiership clubs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish claims self-interest and poor governance are killing Scottish football’s hopes of improvement.

McLeish is frustrated that Scottish Football Association chief football officer Craig Mulholland has reportedly had to dilute prepares for young player quotas to appease five William Hill Premiership clubs.

Mulholland was hoping to ensure teams featured Scotland Under-21 eligible players for an average of 60 minutes per league game and had two on the pitch for each cup tie.

McLeish mentioned: 'That’s damning that he’s having to change his intends to pander to clubs who aren’t really on board with it and don’t really have the best interests of the Scottish national team at heart.

Recent findings suggest that 'I understand why. We have owners from outwith this country. We have managers from outwith this country. They’re in jobs, they’re all fighting for their clubs.

'But why then are those people allowed to be the ones that hold the keys to the future of our country and the development of our national team?

St Mirren boss Craig McLeish believes self-interest at clubs is hampering Scottish football.

'It’s the way governance is set up and we’ve killed ourselves with that because the people who actually have a say in it have, not have no interest but they’ve got self-interest, and there’s a lot of self-interest at the top end.

Industry observers note that 'I just don’t see a way that we can really properly change unless something to do with governance changes and I just don’t ever see that happening. It’s really sad.'.

Although McLeish backs quotas, he fears that would not address the root cause of Scottish football’s problems.

'We always focus at the top end, what our league size is, quotas for young players, a national base,' noted the 36-year-old, who worked in St Mirren’s youth academy before his current role.

It has been revealed that 'We have a fundamental problem that starts at our youngest age groups, at four and five years of age, about how we actually teach kids to play. And until you fix that, you can’t fix the top end of it.

Recent findings suggest that 'It’s crazy some of the stuff that’s going on, the formats, how we teach kids. There’s just a massive lack of education and expertise at the very bottom of our pathway.

'In this country, football’s everyone’s sport and everyone gets access to it but if you take your young kids along to swimming or gymnastics or whatever other sport, you’re there with properly qualified coaches, teachers who have maybe done things at the top levels of that sport.

'We have nothing without the volunteers that work at the bottom end of the grassroots game, but they’re not teaching kids how to play football properly, in my mind.

'And you’re just hoping that they get put with a volunteer coach that can teach them something, that they get in with a really good group at the youngest ages.

'Because that development between the ages of three and eight, if you don’t get that right, you’re dead. You can’t do anything after that point, and we don’t do it well enough. And you’re just chasing yourself and we’ll never catch up.'.

The SFA has been contacted for comment.

And he repaid the new permanent manager’s faith with a dominant aerial display.

Following the game, Heneghan noted: “Standards needed to be raised, I’ll be brutally honest, and as time goes on we’ll get those standards better and better.

Sources indicate that “We’ve just got to keep working and sticking together. It’s a good group and the more we play together we’ll win some points.”.

The 33 year-old’s performance was an example of driving the Reds’ standards forward from the back.

He won more than his fair share of headers and set the tone inside the first 10 minutes with a sliding block to stop a fierce Fleetwood strike from range in their first effort on goal.

Speaking about the importance of breaking their Broadfield Stadium hoodoo and earning a crucial first three points at home in the league, Heneghan stated: “For the group it’s great, obviously they [Crawley] won against Oldham as well so it’s back-to-back wins in the league, which is great for confidence and morale and building on that really.”.

Reflecting on his first league match in six months, the former Fleetwood player added: “Personally, it’s massive just to be back out there playing football and the relief of getting three points, so we’ve got to build on that.

“It’s the best, it’s all I’ve known since I started playing at the age of four. So, I want to continue for as long as possible until the body doesn’t work.”.

Blackwell’s Reds remain unbeaten in his opening three games since taking over the reigns and singled out the performances of Heneghan, Pemi Aderoju and Danilo Orsi in Town’s first league victory since March this year.

Recent findings suggest that speaking in the post-match press conference, Blackwell stated: “I thought Ben Heneghan came in, his first game for six months – I thought he did terrific. I thought [it was] maybe Pemi’s (Aderoju) best game since I’ve been here.

Industry observers note that “[Danilo] Orsi – he’s worked so hard in training and I thought, today, he covered every blade of ground. I thought they all did well. It looked a very good unit today.

According to recent reports, “But I want more. I need more, from certain aspects of the game and we’re hopefully trying to develop that now.”.

Heneghan is only focused on the Reds’ future performances on the pitch and made it clear that the squad understands the manager’s individual and collective expectations.

Sources indicate that he said: “What’s happened has happened and it’s gone now. The manager’s committed until the end of the season so that’s reassuring for everyone. Everyone knows their role and everyone knows what part they’re going to play.”.

Crawley welcome second-placed Barnet to Broadfield on Tuesday night (November 24) and have the chance to climb out of the relegation zone with another win.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:38, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:43.

Kasimpasa will be looking to extend their unbeaten run when they welcome Alanyaspor to Recep Tayyip Erdogan Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts occupy fifth place in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 20 points from 11 matches, while the visitors sit 13th with 12 points and will be desperate to end a difficult run of results after losing their last four games.

Emre Belozoglu's sudden departure to Fenerbahce has not affected Kasimpasa, who have continued their encouraging run of form in recent weeks, putting together a five-match unbeaten streak in all competitions to move into contention for a place in the upper half of the Turkish Super Lig table.

The run began with a 4-1 home victory over Samsunspor, before they followed that result with a 1-0 away win against Eyupspor six days later.

They continued their progress with a 3-1 victory over Corluspor 1947 in the Turkish Cup, although their next league assignment proved considerably more challenging as they held Besiktas to a 2-2 draw at home.

Kasimpasa then produced another impressive performance in their most recent league outing, which was Alfred Schreuder's first game in charge, recording a 2-0 away victory over Gaziantep to make it three wins and a draw in their last four league matches.

The Apaches will therefore be confident of continuing their progress against Alanyaspor, particularly as they have yet to lose at home this season, although they have recorded just one victory, with the other four league games ending in draws.

The hosts will also draw encouragement from their recent record in this fixture, having avoided defeat in their last nine meetings with the visitors, winning seven and drawing two, including each of the last five encounters.

Alanyaspor, meanwhile, have endured a difficult period after making a reasonably encouraging start to the campaign, with their recent defeats leaving them in the bottom half of the standings.

Joao Pereira's side began their latest run of league fixtures with a goalless draw against Erzurumspor before suffering a 3-0 defeat away to Fenerbahce seven days later.

They subsequently lost 2-1 at home to Kocaelispor, with their defensive problems becoming more pronounced when they travelled to face Genclerbirligi, where they were beaten 5-0, suffering their heaviest defeat of the campaign.

Their struggles continued in their most recent league fixture, as they lost 2-0 at home to Trabzonspor, leaving them without a league goal in consecutive matches.

Their 4-1 Turkish Cup victory over 12 Bingolspor offered some encouragement between those league defeats, but the visitors have struggled to transfer that attacking performance into their domestic campaign.

Kasimpasa will be without Elson Mendes, who is suspended for Sunday's encounter, while Godfried Frimpong and Kamil Corekci are also expected to miss out through injury.

Kevin Mouanga, Fousseni Diabate and Mortadha Ben Ouanes are among the players carrying fitness concerns, while Andri Fannar Baldursson is also expected to be unavailable after picking up a muscle injury.

Adrian Benedyczak is expected to lead the attack after establishing himself as the club's leading scorer, with Haris Hajradinovic and John-Jules Rak-Sakyi likely to provide support from behind the striker.

Alanyaspor are expected to be without Paolo Fernandes, who is recovering from a muscle injury, while Fatih Aksoy is also a doubt after picking up an injury.

Pereira could therefore retain much of the side that started against Trabzonspor, with Ruan, Hwang Ui-jo and Ogulcan Usluoglu expected to provide the attacking threat for the visitors.

Kasimpasa possible starting lineup:.

Gianniotis; Winck, Arous, Ilie, Karapo; Jessen, Demirbay; Rak-Sakyi, Hajradinovic, Kol; Benedyczak.

Alanyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Paulo Victor; Nuno Lima, Aliti, Ozyurt; Hadergjonaj, Gezek, Maestro, Ozdemir; Ruan, Hwang, Usluoglu.

Kasimpasa have shown considerably more consistency than their opponents in recent weeks and have also dominated this fixture in recent seasons, which is why we expect the hosts to secure a comfortable home victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the crisp chill of a late November evening in North Lanarkshire, Rangers required a late deflection to prise three vital Scottish Premiership points from the grasp of a resolute and industrious Motherwell side.

With the contest seemingly bound to end 1-1, a potentially significant blip for the visitors in terms of their title aspirations, Ryan Naderi’s 88th-minute effort struck the unfortunate Martin Moormann and looped past goalkeeper Alex Paulsen, inflicting the cruellest of blows on the Steelmen.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

There seemed an almost ritualistic rhythm to Rangers’ recent visits to Fir Park: waves of possession crashing against a disciplined claret-and-amber breakwater, accompanied by the persistent nagging doubt that dominance without ruthlessness invites punishment.

Derek McInnes’s side were living out that exact cautionary tale on their latest visit before Naderi popped up with a crucial late winner.

In a recent development, for the opening 15 minutes, this contest threatened to become a procession. Rangers monopolised the ball and the opening goal arrived after just eight minutes. Motherwell’s defensive structure momentarily frayed under early pressure, allowing centre-back Emmanuel Fernandez to rise unmarked and head home Kim Min-Su’s corner with disarming simplicity.

At that juncture, Motherwell appeared to be unravelling. Within six minutes of falling behind, Alfred Johansson was forced into an early reshuffle when winger Ibrahim Said limped off injured in visible distress to be replaced by Regan Charles-Cook.

According to recent reports, rangers sensed blood. Naderi probed tirelessly, Djeidi Gassama repeatedly cut inside off the left flank to test the Steelmen defence, and Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen was called upon to produce a string of top-class saves to prevent the visitors from establishing an unassailable cushion.

In a recent development, however, Scottish football rarely rewards aesthetic superiority alone. Having weathered the initial storm without conceding a second, the hosts summoned an equaliser from their first corner of the evening in the 21st minute. Emmanuel Longelo rolled a clever short pass to Tom Sparrow, whose curling delivery into the penalty area found Jake Girdwood-Reich entirely unmarked. The Australian defender needed no second invitation, sweeping a composed finish past Ivor Pandur to restore parity against the run of play.

In a recent development, that subtly altered the psychological temperature inside Fir Park. While Rangers continued to dictate proceedings, racking up nearly 20 attempts on goal, their lack of cutting edge in the final third was glaring. Before the interval, Paulsen defied the visitors once more with a superb reflex stop from Nico Raskin in the 41st minute.

According to recent reports, mcInnes’ men pressed forward with renewed urgency after a stern half-time team talk. Seven minutes into the second half, Dan Neil drifted into a pocket of space on the edge of the area and drilled a low effort that whistled agonisingly past the post.

Visible frustration began to creep into Rangers’ ranks passing the hour mark as a combination of misplaced passes and poor finishing drew audible groans from the packed away end.

In a recent development, sensing his team’s grip on the contest loosening, McInnes turned to his bench in the 69th minute, introducing summer signing Kevin Kelsy in place of Gassama to add a greater physical presence in attack alongside Naderi. There was little immediate improvement. Badredine Bouanani raced down the right flank and cut the ball back for Neil, whose shot sailed high and wide.

Motherwell were looking increasingly comfortable and Tawanda Maswanhise tested Pandur from distance as the home side sensed an opportunity to claim something more substantial than a point.

Findlay Curtis was introduced for Rangers and almost made an immediate impact, delivering an excellent cross towards the back post which Naderi was unable to turn home from close range.

Then came another extraordinary intervention from Paulsen. Curtis' effort appeared to have beaten the keeper, who could only palm the ball into the path of Sterling. However, Paulsen recovered magnificently to divert the right-back’s follow-up onto the crossbar. It was a remarkable piece of goalkeeping and, by this stage, it seemed entirely possible that the home side would clinch a share of the spoils.

They were not to be so fortunate.

With two minutes remaining, Rangers finally found the breakthrough their territorial dominance had threatened to deliver. Naderi got his effort away, but Moormann intervened and inadvertently diverted the ball beyond his own goalkeeper. The unfortunate centre-back could do little about the decisive deflection, but the consequences were devastating for Motherwell.

Industry observers note that the travelling Rangers support erupted, relief and celebration combining in equal measure. For McInnes, it was a precious late reward for a side that had made unnecessarily hard work of a match they might have settled long before the closing stages.

The victory extends Rangers' unbeaten run in all competitions to 13 matches and ensures they remain in touch with Celtic, moving back within four points of the league leaders with a game in hand.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:40, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:42.

Konyaspor will be looking to halt their recent slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Besiktas to Medas Konya Buyuksehir Stadyumu on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with eight points from 11 matches, only outside the bottom three on goal difference, while the Black Eagles occupy fifth place with 19 points from 10 games and will be hoping to maintain their push towards the top of the standings.

Konyaspor have endured a difficult run of results in recent weeks, winning just once in their last six league matches and struggling to find consistency in the final third.

Ilhan Palut's side began that sequence with consecutive goalless draws against Kasimpasa and Istanbul Basaksehir before suffering a 1-0 defeat away to Amed SK.

They then recorded a 2-0 home victory over Genclerbirligi, but that proved to be their only success during the period as they suffered consecutive defeats against Galatasaray (4-0) and Samsunspor (1-0).

Konyaspor were particularly disappointing in their defeat away to Samsunspor just before the break, failing to take anything from a match against a side sitting second-bottom and enduring a losing run.

The result further highlighted their struggles in front of goal, with the hosts having scored just six times in their opening 11 league matches, an average of fewer than one per game, while they have failed to find the net in seven of those fixtures.

Konyaspor have scored four of their six goals and collected seven of their eight points on home soil, although they were thrashed by Galatasaray in their last home game and now face a Besiktas side that have beaten them in their last two league meetings.

The hosts did manage to defeat the Black Eagles 1-0 in their most recent encounter, although that victory came in the Turkish Cup.

Besiktas, meanwhile, have enjoyed a more productive campaign, collecting seven wins, one draw and three defeats from their opening 11 league matches to remain within reach of the leading teams, sitting six points behind league leaders Galatasaray.

Vincenzo Italiano's side are also unbeaten in their last three league games, a sequence that began with a 2-0 home victory over Istanbul Basaksehir before they were held to a 2-2 draw by Kasimpasa.

Their subsequent European fixture saw them suffer a 3-2 defeat against Celtic, but they responded positively three days later by recording a convincing 3-0 home win over Genclerbirligi.

Dusan Vlahovic was particularly influential in that victory, scoring twice as the Black Eagles returned to winning ways in the Super Lig and demonstrated the attacking quality that has made them one of the more productive sides in the division, with only four teams scoring more than their 23 goals.

However, the visitors have struggled on the road, winning just one of their five away league matches and failing to win any of their last three, during which they have recorded one draw and two defeats.

Konyaspor will be without Adil Demirbag, who is recovering from a cruciate ligament injury and is expected to remain sidelined for the rest of the season.

Chidozie Awaziem is also unlikely to feature after sustaining a muscle injury, while Marko Jevtovic is working towards regaining full fitness and faces a late assessment.

Ugurcan Yazgili is another concern after picking up a hamstring problem, leaving Palut with defensive and midfield decisions to make.

Mostafa Mohamed, Diogo Goncalves and Ebrima Colley are among the attacking options available to the Konyaspor manager, although Enis Bardhi is expected to miss out through suspension.

Besiktas will be without Umit Akdag, who is recovering from a broken wrist, while Fabio Miretti is also expected to miss the match with a shoulder injury.

Emmanuel Agbadou is not expected to return until later in December as he continues his recovery from a knee problem, while Orkun Kokcu is also sidelined with a foot injury.

Konyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Gungordu; Andzouana, Baniya, Bosluk, Masuaku; Toth, Ibrahimoglu; Colley, Goncalves, Dompe; Mohamed.

Besiktas possible starting lineup:.

Nubel; Murillo, Taylan Bulut, Topcu, R Yilmaz; Ndidi; Trossard, S Ozcan, Olaitan, Fakili; Vlahovic.

Konyaspor have struggled to produce consistent attacking performances this season, and although Besiktas have been inconsistent on the road, their attacking quality should be enough to overcome the hosts' defensive resistance, with Italiano's side expected to secure a comfortable victory in Konya.

Oli McBurnie broke the deadlock in the 92nd minute before completing his brace three minutes later, with the hosts taking full advantage of Brighton being reduced to ten men following Costinha's 89th-minute dismissal.

Morrison's reaction to Hull's opening goal on BBC Radio 5 Live captured the drama of the occasion.

The former striker suggested the Tigers had not necessarily done enough to deserve the breakthrough, but said that would not matter to the home supporters.

He remarked: "This is why you've got to love this beautiful game.

"They do not deserve this. But who cares if they deserve it?

"They have a man in Oli McBurnie who can find the net at times and this could be a massive goal for Hull City.

Industry observers note that albion dominated possession throughout the match and had multiple chances to open the scoring. Diego Gomez could have had a hat-trick and the usually efficient Pascal Gross was also wasteful.

Costinha also had a massive opportunity to put the visitors ahead early on, with the red card compounding a poor afternoon for the Portuguese full-back.

Hull took full advantage and found a way through at the death.

Sources indicate that with time running out, Regan Slater played in Lucas Gourna-Douath – who squared it to Oli McBurnie. The veteran made no mistake, despite Ferdi Kadioglu’s last ditch attempt to save his team.

And there was more to come, with McBurnie tapping home a second in the 95th minute after Mohamed Belloumi beat Maxim De Cuyper and played the ball across goal.

What had looked like a frustrating afternoon for Hull turned into a memorable victory, while Brighton were left to reflect on a costly late sending-off and a dramatic collapse.

Sources indicate that morrison said: “The Brighton players will be disappointed. They were by far the better team. The Hull goalkeeper produced saves like that and had a brilliant game.

“Brighton's finishing wasn't good enough. As much as Konstantinos Tzolakis had a brilliant afternoon, I think Brighton could've done better in front of goal. But credit to Hull.

"No team is going to go toe to toe with Brighton and you have to show them respect and that's what Hull did. They stayed in the game.

"They needed their goalkeeper to have a good game and the defenders to defend well. And when you go and smell danger and smell blood you have to go and take it.

Sources indicate that “Once Brighton went down to ten men this place lifted. The fans got behind and they knew this was their opportunity and they grabbed it with both hands.”.

Industry observers note that the Seagulls remain second in the table but missed a chance to move within three points of leaders Arsenal. Hull, meanwhile, moved up to 11th place.

McInnes believes Naderi's contribution extends far beyond his goals, insisting his work rate should not overshadow the quality of his all-round performances.

Sources indicate that “Ryan’s game is really strong at the minute. He looks like a very confident boy and so he should be,” McInnes said. “Wrongly now, when you think of Ryan or people ask me, it’s about him knocking his pan in. His pressing is unbelievable and he’s a massive horse up there. He runs and works and puts people under pressure.

Industry observers note that “He looks tired but his performances are always strong. But he gets goals and has an influence. In that system tonight, his was the most important position for us, in terms of running channels and getting hold of the ball. His touch was one of a really confident player and he led the line brilliantly. It was a proper number nine performance.”.

Recent findings suggest that on his side’s performance, McInnes added: “We got our just rewards in the game, absolutely. I thought it was a very good, strong performance and I’ve been told that every one of my outfield players had a shot tonight. I’ve never known a team who practice so much shooting, and crossing and finishing during the week.

“It was the only thing missing for us, I thought it was a top class performance. We mixed the game up well. Our press was strong and we were aggressive. I’m just disappointed it took so long to get the winning goal.”.

Deflated Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson admitted his side struggled to cope with Rangers' early intensity, but felt the early loss of Ibrahim Remarked to injury was a major blow before his side ran out of energy in the closing stages.

Recent findings suggest that “They are title challengers and we have a really tough start to the game,” he mentioned. “They put us down. When we win it back, we give it away again. They get momentum. I don't think it's a free kick that they get before their first goal, but we should defend much, much better on that defensive corner kick.

Industry observers note that “In that moment, in the same period, we lose Ibrahim [Said], which is really tough for us, given that the players we have on the bench, many of them in the offensive positions, are not ready to play more than 30 to 45 minutes with high intensity. So it was tough to lose him, and therefore, it's strong of the players to come back and score a goal from a set play and equalise.

“But the last 15-20 minutes, Rangers take completely over and we don't have energy enough in that moment to keep the intensity up.”.

Jakirovic admitted his side had been made to suffer before the break, with the goalkeeper producing several key saves.

Speaking to Sky Sports, he stated: "We played against an excellent team today, very high intensity. In the first half we survived and Konstantinos Tzolakis saved us four or five times.

According to recent reports, "We had more stability in the second half. We won 2-0 and I'm extremely happy because we wait almost three months [for another win] which is unbelievable.

Jakirovic also felt his side had taken advantage of the opportunity presented by Costinha's 89th-minute dismissal.

McBurnie reveals daughter's lucky rabbit.

McBurnie was quick to acknowledge the contribution of his goalkeeper, admitting Hull had ridden their luck against a Brighton side he described as a top team.

Industry observers note that speaking to Sky Sports, he stated: "We haven't lost a game at home. They are a top team and we knew it was going to be tough.

The striker also revealed the unusual good-luck charm he had taken onto the pitch – a toy rabbit belonging to his daughter.

"My daughter when I leave for work every game she makes me take something with me for good luck," he explained.

In a recent development, "Today it was her bun bun because that's what she had in her hand. It's all good fun and I'm sure she will be happy with that one.".

McBurnie was equally full of praise for Tzolakis, jokingly referring to him as 'the cat' when speaking to Match of the Day.

Recent findings suggest that "It's his job. That's what he's there for. The cat was brilliant today and we are lucky to have him," he said.

"He's kept us in a few games this year.

"Brighton are a top team and we knew we were going to be suffering and ride our luck at times, but with a bit of luck and with the cat in net we rode our luck and stayed in the game.".

'The football for the goals was brilliant'.

"Buzzing for the boys because we haven't won for a while," he said.

In a recent development, following a more encouraging performance against Dartford on Tuesday evening, Bridges knew that nothing less than three points would do if they were to stand any chance of remaining a Step 3 side next season. And it was the home side who started on the front foot, dominating much of the first half and creating a number of opportunities. Noel Leighton, Reece Hallard, Hayden Velvick and Charlie Bennett all went close inside the opening 25 minutes, but none could find a way past Cheshunt goalkeeper Rex Porter.

It has been revealed that against the run of play, however, the visitors took the lead. Hayden Neathey conceded a needless free-kick just outside the penalty area, and Joe Re stepped up to curl the ball past Sam Roberts. That familiar sinking feeling descended over Jubilee Field, and despite having enjoyed the better of the half, Bridges went into the interval a goal behind.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But this time, there was no heads dropping. Bridges continued where they had left off, and their positive approach was eventually rewarded.

After seeing an attempted lob saved by Porter, Leighton and his teammates finally found a way through, with the lively Hayden Velvick restoring parity. Picking up the ball on the right-hand side of the penalty area, the winger unleashed an effort which somehow found its way past Porter at his near post. However it went in, nobody in amber and black was complaining, and Bridges were back on level terms.

Sources indicate that the hosts continued to press for a winner, and debutant Jadyn Dundas should have put them ahead just minutes after coming off the bench. Arriving at the back post with the goal at his mercy, he was unable to get his feet sorted out in time to convert. What then followed was an end-to-end contest, with Sam Granville striking the crossbar for Cheshunt before Leighton and Velvick both saw efforts bravely blocked by visiting defenders.

Industry observers note that this time, though, Bridges were not to be denied. Cheshunt failed to deal with the danger inside their own penalty area, and after Porter could only parry an initial deflected effort, the ball fell kindly into the path of Noel Leighton. The striker made no mistake from close range, sending Jubilee Field into celebration and, more importantly, putting Bridges 2-1 ahead.

The home side looked relatively comfortable heading towards the final whistle, but injury time brought one final scare. An almighty scramble inside the Bridges six-yard box threatened to produce a late Cheshunt equaliser, with the visitors seemingly doing everything they could to force the ball over the line. Somehow, the Bridges defence stood firm and managed to clear their lines before the referee finally blew for full-time.

There was an enormous sigh of relief around Jubilee Field as Three Bridges secured just their third league victory of the season. A hugely important result for Jamie Crellin's side, and one which could prove to be a turning point in their season.

If the great escape is to become a reality, Jubilee Field must now become a fortress, starting next Saturday afternoon when Wingate & Finchley visit for another crucial encounter.

Bridges team: Roberts, Ferreira, J Hallard (Irving 75), Adeyinka, Neathey, Leighton (C), R Hallard (Dundas 65), Malone, Saunders, Velvick, Bennett (Idowu-Johnson 87).

Unused Subs: Villavicencio, Przybylo.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 22:07.
  • Trabzonspor will look to extend their winning run in the league to seven games when they host bottom-placed Eyupspor at Papara Park on Sunday.
  • The Black Sea outfit sit second in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 25 points from 11 matches, three behind league leaders Galatasaray, while the visitors are 18th with just three points, five adrift of safety.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 22:07.

Trabzonspor will look to extend their winning run in the league to seven games when they host bottom-placed Eyupspor at Papara Park on Sunday.

The Black Sea outfit sit second in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 25 points from 11 matches, three behind league leaders Galatasaray, while the visitors are 18th with just three points, five adrift of safety.

Thomas Reis has made an excellent start to his reign, winning all six of his league games in charge, with the latest victory coming in a 2-0 away triumph over Alanyaspor just before the international break, as Wagner Pina opened the scoring in the 17th minute before Muhammed Salah doubled their advantage in the 34th.

That result represented a strong response to their 1-0 defeat to Freiburg in the Conference League, which brought an end to their seven-game winning streak across all competitions.

Trabzonspor will now look to begin another run of victories, and their attacking and defensive records suggest they have every reason to be confident, having scored 26 goals, the fourth-highest tally in the division, while conceding just eight, the fewest in the league, as they build a strong foundation in their pursuit of a first league title since 2021-22.

The hosts have also won all five of their league games at home this season, and another victory would see them match the club's best start to a home league campaign, last achieved in 1984-85.

Meanwhile, Eyupspor are in deep trouble after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Kocaelispor last time out, their eighth consecutive league loss and the ninth time in 11 matches this season that they have failed to score in the division.

No other side has conceded more goals than Eyupspor this season, with their tally standing at 30, while they have also scored just three times, the fewest in the league.

Mustafa Dalci mentioned after the defeat to Kocaelispor that his side are entering a period in which they must start collecting points, but their prospects look bleak ahead of another difficult away fixture, particularly as they have conceded a league-high 19 goals on their travels.

Their head-to-head record against Trabzonspor offers little encouragement either, with Eyupspor yet to win any of their four previous meetings, drawing one and losing three, while they have failed to score in all four encounters.

Trabzonspor form (all competitions):.

Eyupspor Turkish Super Lig form:.

Reis has several absentees to contend with, including defender Chibuike Nwaiwu, who is suspended after accumulating yellow cards.

Batagov, Franculino Dju, Ruslan Malinovskyi and Okay Yokuslu are also expected to miss out, although a number of injured players have returned to training, with Ernest Muci, Tim Jabol-Folcarelli and Wagner Pina all potentially available after recovering from their respective problems.

Aral Simsir is also being assessed ahead of the match, while Cihan Canak and Onuralp Cevikkan remain injury concerns, leaving Reis with several selection decisions to make before naming his squad.

Eyupspor, meanwhile, have their own injury problems, with Talha Ulvan, Omer Ceyhan, Ahmed Abdullahi, Bilal Boutobba, Lenny Pintor and Simone Giordano all listed as unavailable or doubtful.

Dalci could therefore be forced to make changes, particularly in defence and attack, although the visitors are expected to retain much of the starting XI that faced Kocaelispor before the international break.

Trabzonspor possible starting lineup:.

Onana; Pina, Savic, Cenk Ozkacar, Cabral; Fabinho, Tufan; Salah, Muci, Saviolo; Onuachu.

Eyupspor possible starting lineup:.

Moldovan; Yavuz, El Yamiq, Jules, Yasar; Massanga, Akman; Michalak, Sabiri, Yao; Abdullahi.

Trabzonspor have the league's best defensive record, an impressive winning run, home advantage and a dominant head-to-head record against Eyupspor, all of which point towards a comfortable victory for the hosts, who should also be capable of keeping a clean sheet against the division's lowest-scoring side.

#60793. How Mykhailo Mudryk's unsolicited interview turned into a moany mess: With gaffes galore - including his Arsenal 'dream' - the £89m man hasn't endeared himself to either Spurs or Chelsea, writes KIERAN GILL

How Mykhailo Mudryk's unsolicited interview turned into a moany mess: With gaffes galore - including his Arsenal 'dream' - the £89m man hasn't endeared himself to either Spurs or Chelsea, writes KIERAN GILL

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1398 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:05 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:02 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Not for the first time, Mykhailo Mudryk was in a good position, and displayed poor judgement.
  • Criticising London for its 20mph speed limit, saying 'it's hard to follow these rules, however much I'd like to' after his latest driving ban, and how the wealthy are taxed 45 per cent on these shores.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 07:05 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:02 EST, 20 November 2026.

Not for the first time, Mykhailo Mudryk was in a good position, and displayed poor judgement. This time, it was away from the pitch, in a two-hour, sit-down, tell-all interview involving gaffes galore.

Criticising London for its 20mph speed limit, saying 'it's hard to follow these rules, however much I'd like to' after his latest driving ban, and how the wealthy are taxed 45 per cent on these shores.

Naming 'Ukraine' when asked which is the best city in the world – he may have misunderstood the question, so we will let him off with that one – and admitting he signed contracts without reading them while denouncing the deals done by his former representatives.

Then there was his interviewer, a grinning chap called Dmitry Gordon, asking him if he speaks to his four cats in English, and why he wears earrings, and if girls send him pictures. Bizarre enquiries. Had Chelsea or Tottenham Hotspur known about this interview happening – and Daily Mail Sport understands they were not informed – then we cannot imagine either Premier League club would have liked such lines of questioning.

It has been revealed that nor will they, or their fanbases, be too fond of the 25-year-old Ukrainian explaining his move to England in the first place. He revealed how much he wanted to play for Arsenal, describing it as his 'dream' as he blamed his old agent for pushing him to Chelsea for the money.

What was supposed to be an opportunity for Mudryk to tell his side of the story, after a doping ban which cost him two years of his career, resembled more of a moany mess.

Mykhailo Mudryk's interview was a bizarre mess and indicated his utter naivety.

The Ukrainian winger was given a one-year driving ban in December last year.

By the end, the seriousness of his allegations against the Ukrainian national team with regard to his failed drugs test were softened by the nonsensical own goals much more likely to set social media alight.

Such as the naivety of a Chelsea player on loan at Tottenham appearing to pine for Arsenal, and saying he still wants to win the Ballon d'Or, which is only ever an admission prone to being patronised online even if a sign of his ambition.

A reminder: Mudryk signed for Chelsea from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023 for £89million. He struggled, never looked like a winger worth such a fee. Frighteningly fast, but did not know how to use his weaponry properly in the Premier League. Graham Potter was his manager when he arrived. A few months later, it was Frank Lampard. A month after that, Mauricio Pochettino.

Then he was suspended for two years, during which time Chelsea supported his insistence that he was innocent and continued to pay his salary, believed to be worth around £100,000 per week.

Recent findings suggest that while banned, he turned up in Wroclaw, Poland the day before the 2025 Conference League final, apparently there to collect his medal in case Chelsea won. Enzo Maresca was unaware, only learning that he was in the city when we told him at his pre-match press conference.

Upon Mudryk's return to football in the summer of 2026, Chelsea decided he needed to leave on loan, and another one of the Premier League's big-six sides gave him his second chance.

According to recent reports, tottenham called. Brentford, Brighton, Leeds and Coventry were among those also willing, but Roberto De Zerbi promised to give him a platform to prove his talents.

He appeared once, as a 74th-minute substitute away at Nottingham Forest in September. Then he disappeared, injured, and his only sighting since has been here, on YouTube, as a 'Guest of Gordon'.

Chelsea will also be unhappy about Mudryk's interview and were not informed about it.

Mykhailo Mudryk's is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.

Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.

He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'.

And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission.

'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' remarked Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London.

Sources indicate that 'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a massive club, like the other clubs, not less at all.'.

Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition.

According to recent reports, 'He has no responsibility in this part,' stated De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play.

It has been revealed that 'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.'.

Mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return.

Recent findings suggest that 'The proposal was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' said De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.'.

While there should be sympathy with Mudryk, who had to bite his tongue while banned and spending what he described as 'millions' on trying to clear his name, he made a poor choice in the platform chosen to finally speak up.

At one stage, he is asked bluntly whether he considered killing himself. 'No, that's not a way out,' he replied. The title of the video on YouTube, unhelpfully, mentions 'suicidal thoughts' regardless of his answer.

Mudryk may have thought it would help to talk so openly, especially to clarify those he holds responsible for the two years he lost as a footballer.

But he hardly endeared himself to his current club, Tottenham, or to his parent club, Chelsea, to whom he is still contracted into the 2030s.

In a recent development, he likened them to chaos, explaining: 'I came to a Chelsea that was, and perhaps still is, in the middle of a rebuild. It's not the Chelsea that existed under the previous owners, which was stable, had a clear system, coaches, without this constant galloping who knows where.'.

In a recent development, such comments are unlikely to be well received when read by the club's hierarchy, while he also remarked on Chelsea's managerial merry-go-round: 'The coaches themselves don't know what tactics they'll play. They come to the club and try one set of tactics. Whether it works or not, they try another.'.

According to recent reports, when Mudryk returns from his ankle injury, he will have to hope his football can do the talking. After this, neither Tottenham nor Chelsea are likely to want him to speak again any time soon.
