Celtic made light work of St Mirren at the weekend as they ran out 4-1 winners on Saturday afternoon to maintain their lead at the Scottish Premiership.

Three goals in nine first-half minutes from Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (33), Camilo Duran (40) and Luke McCowan (42) put the hosts on course for a comfortable victory, before captain Callum McGregor added to the scoreline in the second period (63). A Killian Phillips penalty (69) provided a consolation for the visitors.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recent findings suggest that the win keeps Celtic four points clear at the top of the table after second-placed Rangers won 2-1 at Motherwell later in the evening kick-off. But what did their win over St Mirren tell us about Celtic’s hopes of winning a sixth successive league title come May?

Graham Falk was at Parkhead to cover proceedings. These are his three key takeaways from Celtic’s win vs St Mirren:.

Mika Baur’s injury looks like it may rule him out for up to 10 weeks and is clearly a big blow for Celtic. The young German has been one of their most impressive performers this season. With Benjamin Nygren also absent, Luke McCowan was handed his first start since September 20.

It has been revealed that forced to delete his social media account to escape personal abuse from sections of the online support just a few short weeks ago, it would have been hard to blame McCowan had he sunk into his shell when an audible groan greeted one of his early misplaced passes at Parkhead. But to McCowan’s credit, he did quite the opposite, and scored Celtic’s clinching third goal just before half-time.

According to recent reports, of course, one swallow doesn’t make a summer, but it’ll take a major weight off his shoulders, and could benefit Celtic with Baur out for a while. The ex-Dundee skipper will admit himself that he’s not been at the level expected this season. But, as proven by his 23 goal contributions across Celtic’s last two title-winning seasons, he’s shown previously that he can play an crucial role.

He’ll never be viewed as someone who will take Celtic to the next level, but he can take confidence from his performance and give O’Neill a valuable option as he awaits Nygren and Baur’s return to full fitness.

In a recent development, in his previous stint as Celtic manager, the veteran boss loved to play with a front two. However, more out of necessity, he’s almost exclusively opted for a front three over the last 12 months. Previous managers Ange Postecoglou and Brendan Rodgers both moulded their side that way, and O’Neill has stuck with it. It’s had its doubters, though, with some calling for him to partner Kasper Hogh with Duran, rather than shifting the Colombian out on the wing to accommodate him.

But did the front three that started against St Mirren show a way forward for O’Neill? Starting Jota and Yang either side of Duran for the first time, the trio were a constant threat throughout for Celtic, who looked a more free-flowing outfit offensively than they have for several weeks.

Recent findings suggest that “Yang is something else for us at the moment,” mentioned O’Neill post-match. “Duran is a top, top quality centre-forward, and Jota is still trying to get up to the speed of the game. But Yang is so strong, he made the first goal for us, and what he does for us defensively is just amazing when you consider he is a wide player.”.

Industry observers note that it was the main question before, during and after the game, in the stands and in the press room. The mystery surrounding Haissem Hassan. Where was he? One of Celtic’s big summer signings, he was left out of the matchday squad for the second successive game, putting the rumours into overdrive.

In a recent development, ahead of the game, O’Neill had quashed suggestions that the Egyptian was omitted from the squad for their last game because he was ‘unpopular’ with other members of his Celtic squad. However, his absence against St Mirren at the weekend was simply due to “rotation”. Hmm.

They didn’t miss him too much on the field, with Celtic rolling to a comfortable win over their Paisley counterparts. However, while no one can say Duran hasn’t repaid the £6million fee shelled out on him, the combined £20million spent on Hogh and Hassan is rightly being brought into question. We’re almost into December: one can’t get into the squad, and the other hasn’t scored a goal in over 1000 minutes. Surely O’Neill expected much more bang for his buck, even if he won’t admit it publicly.

In a recent development, brighton actually played well for long periods but tired as the match progressed. Fabian Hurzeler’s men started as the team more likely to score with Yasin Ayari, Costinha and Georginio all going close in the first half.

Ayari then rattled the bar from a Diego Gomez cross and Georgino's follow-up effort was well saved by Hull keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Sources indicate that brighton players were clearly frustrated as they went down the tunnel at halftime and started fast after the break. Pascal Gross saw a left footed effort blocked by the excellent Tzolakis and Gomez fired wide when well placed on 51 minutes.

Jack Hinshelwood, Charalampos Kostoulas and Yankuba Minteh were introduced but Hull came closest as Sorba Thomas’ mis-hit cross deceived Bart Verbruggen and hit the bar.

Kostoulas then saw a chipped effort cleared off the line but Brighton were punished after Costinha’s dismissal. McBurnie’s late double - both from close range - was a painful one to take.

They remain second in the table on 22 points from 11 matches, six behind leaders Arsenal.

According to recent reports, bart Verbruggen - 6: He conceded five for the Dutch against the Germans during the international break and another two here. Neither of McBurnies were his fault to be fair.

Costinha - 3: Missed a golden chance on 18 minutes as he sidefooted wide of the post. Booked for a cynical foul on Thomas and then another booking on 89 minutes saw him dismissed. Quite silly really and a poor game for the Portuguese.

Lewis Dunk - 5: Caught in possession in the early stages and passing not as accurate as usual.

Luka Vuskovic - 6: Booked on 34 minutes for a foul and then kicking the ball away. He had a tough battle with McBurnie.

Industry observers note that olivier Boscagli - 5: Maintained his ever-present record and delivered a steady performance at left back with some nice distribution. Replaced by Minteh on 67.

Pascal Gross - 5: The German should have had another assists to his tally as he set-up the Costinha chance on 18 minutes. Saw a left footed effort beaten away by Tzolakis after the break.

According to recent reports, chema - 6: The young Spaniard does the basics well and was good for the most part. Ran out of gas in the later stages. He was booked for a foul on Coyle.

Diego Gomez - 7: Fizzed a delightful cross into the box on 13 minutes which somehow just eluded everyone. He also supplied the cross that saw Ayari rattled the bar. Should have scored on 51 when he flashed an angled effort wide of the far post. Replaced by Kadioglu on 80.

Industry observers note that yasin Ayari - 6: Saw his first-time sliding effort well saved by Tzolakis. He probably should have scored. Rattled the bar with a brilliant first time effort on 36 minutes. He got into the positions but just not ruthless enough. Replaced by Hinshelwood on 66 minutes.

It has been revealed that max De Cuyper - 6: Delivered an accurate cross to tee-up Ayari's major chance on 14 minutes. Lacked the cutting edge needed to breakthrough this stubborn Hull team.

In a recent development, georginio - 6: Selected ahead of Kostoulas and forced a sharp save from Tzolakis on 31 minutes with crisp right footed effort. Tzolakis then denied him on 38 minutes with an even better save. A solid outing for the Frenchman and his start since the opening day of the season against Villa. Replaced by Kostoulas on 66.

A statistic has been doing the rounds regarding Ruben Amorim’s league record with AC Milan, which is gathering some attention.

Sources indicate that his style of play is open to criticism, his selections are controversial, his words are regularly quite strong and he’s often called into question at the first sign of failure. For Amorim, his first months with the Rossoneri have been a rollercoaster ride.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been ups and downs: things have been better domestically, culminating in a derby victory over Inter, but in the Europa League the one win from four games means the Rossoneri currently sit outside the playoff zone.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, there is a key bit of data to contextualise things. With 24 points in his first 11 Serie A matches, Amorim is averaging 2.18 points per game, the result of seven wins, three draws, and one defeat.

Industry observers note that it is the highest ever for a Milan coach in the three-point era, ahead of Stefano Pioli, Carlo Ancelotti and Massimiliano Allegri. Looking at coaches with at least five stints in the Italian top flight, only Antonio Conte boasts a better figure than the Portuguese coach, with 2.21 points per game.

This is obviously an unfair comparison, given that the former Napoli coach’s points average takes into account all 279 of his Serie A games – with spells at Atalanta, Juventus, Inter and Napoli – compared to just 11 for the former United manager.

However, it is a testament to the excellent work done thus far by Amorim and his staff. Even more so in a season in which the decision was made to undertake a revolution in several respects, to relaunch a team and a fan base that had been burned by the collapse of last season.

Sources indicate that gerry Cardinale and the ownership made significant investments during the last transfer window, spending €70m on Goncalo Ramos and €50m on Diego Moreira, plus €25m on Mario Gila. This is also why Milan fans have high expectations for Amorim’s era.

Recent findings suggest that to date, the average from these first 11 games project the Rossoneri to land around 83 points by the end of the season. Last year, Inter won the Scudetto with 87 points, and 71 were needed to finish fourth, the minimum target set by the owners.

Allegri’s Milan stopped at 70 points, despite a strong start to the season that even fuelled a few Scudetto dreams for a few months. That start, however, was inferior to this season: a year ago, after 11 matchdays, AC Milan had 22 points, two fewer than under Amorim.

It is an encouraging beginning to the newly introduced era that fans hope will translate into concrete results, perhaps even the Scudetto, a target declared by owner Cardinale as a real aim, as unrealistic as it may have seemed before a ball was kicked.

Amorim is trying to convey his vision of football and instil a more European mentality in his team, and the numbers so far – at least in the league – seem to prove him right. To find a better start to a season one must rewind to 2022-23, when Milan had 26 points from 11 games under Pioli.

Ruben Amorim has the highest points-per-game average of any #ACMilan coach in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era: 2.18 over 11 matches.

Among all coaches with 5+ stints in the league during that period, only Antonio Conte (2.21) has a higher average.

[via @OptaPaolo] pic.twitter.com/jwPLgVw0z7.

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 19, 2026.

Speaking of Pioli, in the specific ranking of Milan coaches with the highest points average – led by Amorim, as mentioned – the coach who led the Rossoneri to their 19th Scudetto (2021-22) occupies second place at 2.02 points per game in 183 Serie A matches.

Pioli also achieved the best start in Milan’s history: in the Scudetto year, he earned 31 points from the opening 11 games, the result of 10 wins and 1 draw, with a record average of 2.82 points per game.

Industry observers note that in third place among Milan coaches with the highest points average is Ancelotti, with 1.95 points in 283 Serie A games as Milan coach. Allegri is just off the podium, with 1.91 points in 172 games across his two spells at the club.

To compare Amorim with two of his compatriots who recently worked at Milanello, Paulo Fonseca averaged just 1.59 points per game from 17 games, while Sergio Conceicao fared slightly better with 1.71 points in 21 games.

In a recent development, in short, Amorim’s performance is encouraging, but still relative given the very limited sample size. A crucial month is now beginning for Milan: a seven-game tour de force before Christmas that will reveal a lot about the true ambitions of the coach and his team, with form in Europe to fix.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

“Because Kostoulas came back from the international break with a small concern,” said Hurzeler when asked why Georginio started ahead of Kostoulas.

“Therefore we had to make this decision, it wasn't a tactical decision, we had to take care of the health of the player.

”It's just a small glitch, he came back from being with Greece, so something was there, but he didn't feel like 100 per cent.”.

Hull pounced at the death as Oli McBurnie struck twice in added time to snatch a 2-0 victory against high-flying Brighton at the MKM Stadium.

Hurzeler’s side were dominant but could not find a way through, thwarted on several occasions by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Their push for an eighth victory of the season was then halted by Joao Costinha’s dismissal a minute from time and, from there, the wheels came off.

McBurnie bundled home a fine Hull move two minutes into stoppage time and the Tigers were not done there as the striker buried his fourth goal in as many matches to lift his side up to 11th.

It has been revealed that hurzeler added: "For 65 minutes we showed a good performance then we dropped our intensity, levels and standards. In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon a frustrating game but we have to keep going.

"We will analyse it. That's the process we follow. I always emphasize keep staying humble. We have to outwork the opponent otherwise the opponents are too good in the Premier League and that's what we have to do better next time.".

Brighton, for the first time this season, seemed to run out of gas in the closing stages and the the Costinha sending off tipped the balance in Hull’s favour.

Sources indicate that hurzeler noted: "Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role. We made a decision, at that moment, a wrong decision, but we will analyse it.

“My team was desperate to win it, of course, in certain elements be more patient, be more disciplined, be more structured.

“That's what we missed, not only in the last minutes, also in the minutes before, and again, we will analyse it and make it better.”.

I was at the game played in bitterly cold North Lanarkshire conditions. Here are some of the things I spotted.

It has been revealed that whisper it in hushed tones... but this is the type of game that teams who go on to clinch silverware usually grind out. The expected goals tally of both sides show the tale of the tape, where not too dissimilar to Rangers’ 1-0 at Ibrox last time out, Derek McInnes’ side battered on the door without getting through.

In a recent development, motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen was doing his best ‘you shall not pass’ Gandalf impression, but much like The Balrog dragging the grey wizard from Lord of the Rings into the abyss, eventually his resistance was broken. It was messy but Rangers cared not as they got their winner just before a minimal amount of stoppage time was added on. It’s a clash teams of the recent past in Govan coughed points up in and making it 13 unbeaten domestically will be of great satisfaction to boss McInnes.

In a recent development, motherwell under Alfred Johansson have set their stall out as a side who want to dominate the ball but that hasn’t happened in either home game against Rangers or Celtic. Both sides of the Old Firm have come to Fir Park and been able to dictate play, Martin O’Neill’s side winning 2-0 last month, having controlled proceedings with well over 60% possession. This was much the same albeit the Fir Park defence stood valiantly until they were eventually overwhelmed, Rangers enjoying just under that 60% mark in terms of time on the ball.

Motherwell fans, and supporters of other provincial clubs, have been used to these types of games against Glasgow’s massive two over the years. It’s a defensive stand that more often than not ends in defeat, but it’s more of a shock to the system for Motherwell, given what they have built over the last 18 months. Rangers’ winner was perhaps harsh with the effort put in but the amount of chances coughed up proved there could be little complaints over their visitors claiming all three points. Key playmaker Ibrahim Said looked visibly emotional after being subbed in the first half with injury and that will be of major concern to boss Johansson, with much of his side’s good attacking play usually involving the Nigerian.

Sources indicate that since replacing an injured Lawrence Shankland last time out versus Motherwell, Ryan Naderi has been a man transformed. He bundled home the winner off defender Martin Moormann here to make it 11 goal contributions in as many games. Questions over quality were abundant last term upon his arrival from Hansa Rostock but he has been vital for McInnes this term.

Sources indicate that amid long-term blows to Shankland and Youssef Chermiti, Naderi has firmly made himself Rangers’ main man in attack. Any striker coming into the team would need to play alongside him as it’s hard to see how they function without him. It might be unconventional at times but Naderi’s pressing and knack of being in the right place at the right time is proving invaluable.

Recent findings suggest that this clash between Motherwell and Rangers was the first time since Opta records began in season 2005/06 that there was not one Scottish player in the starting line-up of a top-flight match. As conversations continue over development of young talent in our country, it’s perhaps inevitable it became a talking point across analysis of the match.

In a recent development, let’s get off our high horses for a minute though as the conversation with this particular game needs more nuance. Alex Lowry and Stephen O’Donnell are regular starters for Motherwell but both were unavailable, while club captain Paul McGinn is only recently back from long-term injury. James Penrice would likely have been a starter for Rangers had he been fully fit while Findlay Curtis did get on to make a key impact in the winner. Callum Hendry offered more bite to the home attack at the other end. All of that is not to say a lack of development Scottish talent isn’t an problem, it is, but perhaps this stat isn’t the platform to build that argument from.

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 22:07.

BB Erzurumspor will be looking to end their recent losing run when they welcome Goztepe to Kazim Karabekir Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 12th in the Turkish Super Lig standings after 11 matches, while the visitors occupy 10th place and will be hoping to bounce back from their latest defeat to maintain their push towards the upper half of the table.

Erzurumspor had enjoyed an encouraging spell before their recent setbacks, recording victories over Eyupspor and Gaziantep, as well as a draw with Alanyaspor and a win against Samsunspor, to put together a four-game unbeaten run and move away from the lower reaches of the standings.

However, their momentum was checked when they suffered a 3-1 home defeat against Corum before losing 2-1 away to Caykur Rizespor in their most recent league outing before the international break.

Erzurumspor took the lead against Rizespor through Ibrahim Diabate, but they were unable to hold on to their advantage as the hosts turned the contest around, leaving Serkan Ozbalta's side with consecutive defeats after they had collected 10 points from their preceding four matches.

Despite those setbacks, the hosts will be encouraged by their home performances this season, having beaten Konyaspor, Eyupspor and Samsunspor while suffering defeats against Galatasaray and Corum, the latter being their most recent appearance in front of their supporters.

They will be keen to rediscover the defensive organisation that helped them secure those three victories without conceding, particularly against a Goztepe side that has demonstrated considerable attacking quality in recent weeks.

This will be the fifth Super Lig meeting between the sides, with Erzurumspor picking up two wins, drawing one and losing one of the previous four, although they have lost their last two encounters against the visitors, one in the Turkish Cup and the other in the second division.

Goztepe, meanwhile, had been enjoying an impressive run of results before their latest setback, winning four consecutive league matches as part of a six-game unbeaten streak to establish themselves in the top half of the table.

Stanimir Stoilov's side began that sequence with a 4-0 away victory over Eyupspor before recording a 2-1 win against Kocaelispor and a 2-0 home triumph over Corum.

The visitors then produced one of their most impressive performances of the campaign by defeating Fenerbahce 2-1 away from home.

However, their winning streak came to an end just before the break when they suffered a 2-1 home defeat against Istanbul Basaksehir, with Juan finding the net but the hosts ultimately unable to prevent their opponents from taking all three points.

Goztepe nevertheless have an away unbeaten run to protect, with Goz Goz having gone four games without defeat on the road, winning their last three and drawing the other.

Goztepe SK Turkish Super Lig form:.

Erzurumspor are not expected to have any major suspension concerns heading into the match, although there have been conflicting reports regarding the fitness of several players, including Gyrano Kerk and Festy Ebosele, who are both included in some predicted lineups despite being listed as injury concerns elsewhere.

Ibrahim Diabate is expected to retain his place in attack after scoring in the recent defeat against Rizespor, while Miguel Cardoso, Brandon Baiye and Elisha Owusu are likely to feature in midfield as the hosts look to improve their attacking output.

Goztepe could be without Furkan Bayir and Ogun Bayrak, who have both been reported as injury doubts, while Ibrahim Sabra is continuing his recovery from an ankle injury after returning to training.

Juan is expected to lead the visitors' attacking line alongside Janderson, with Alexis Antunes likely to operate behind the front two as Goz Goz look to maintain their attacking threat.

BB Erzurumspor possible starting lineup:.

Taskiran; Ebosele, Ovacikli, Gerxhaliu, Mujakic, Giorbelidze; Kerk, Owusu, Baiye, Cardoso; Diabate.

Goztepe SK possible starting lineup:.

Ozcimen; Bokele, Godoi, Altikardes; Kurtulan, Rhaldney, Miroshi, Akonnor; Antunes; Juan, Janderson.

Erzurumspor will be eager to take advantage of their home support after consecutive defeats, but Goztepe have demonstrated greater attacking consistency in recent weeks, and we expect Stoilov's side to return to winning ways with a narrow victory.

#60782. Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1652 w)

Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1652 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1. These networks are among the stiffest found in the cytoskeleton and can generate large pushing stresses against stationary obstacles2,3,4,5. When grown against a controlled opposing stress in an atomic force microscope6 or inside the cell7, branched networks alter their own architecture to adapt their compressional stiffness to their environment, but the underpinnings of their mechanics and adaptability are unclear. Here we show that their high density and low connectivity place them outside the scope of standard elastic network models for actin. We show that they are instead dominated by the proliferation of interfilament contacts under compression. This places branched actin in the same category as undercoordinated fibrous materials such as sheep’s wool. When the network is grown under force, filaments entangle as if knitted together and trap contacts in their structure. Trapped contacts have a similar role as crosslinkers in rigidifying the network and are thus key to its active adaptive mechanics.

Roberts put Bognor in the lead as his run down the left saw him beat his marker before coolly sliding it under Rhys Forster in the Hayes goal on eight minutes.

Amari Fashanu won a corner for the visitors with his low strike but Benny Read headed it out. Liam Ferdinand created an opening but missed his chace in front of goal.

According to recent reports, for the Rocks, Henry Nevill hooked a cross in from the left but Callum Laycock looped it up into the air with his head. Lennie Smith sped down the right but his cross-shot was saved.

Bognor extended their lead on 25 minutes when Roberts' shot was pushed out only as far as McDonald, who diverted it into the net on the rebound, despite Forster getting something on it.

From McDonald's corner, Tommy Block was denied in a crowded penalty area. On 38 minutes Joshua Edwards had to receive treatment as he took a bash to the head in a challenge with Laycock.

Smith got on the breakaway for Bognor and he fed McDonald, who struck a shot wide along the deck. Harry Grant blasted over as Hayes were very wasteful in front of goal.

Four minutes after the break, a fierce ball in from Dernell Wynter saw Ferdinand divert it in from close range to make it 2-1.

Shroll got another dangerous ball into the box but Amos Nasha's header was directed straight at Tommy Scott. Shroll went into the book for a shoulder barge into the back of Smith. Kaya Tshaka's free-kick picked out Block but his header was saved.

Recent findings suggest that tshaka swiped at a chance of his own and he had to come off injured. Ethan Robb replaced him.

Recent findings suggest that nevill blazed a cross from the left too high before Fashanu hit a curling effort with his right foot and Scott palmed it out. Fashanu hit a corner deep towards the back post with Shroll under it, but Laycock and Scott combined to keep it out.

Nasha did well to pass the ball to Ferdinand and he hit the right post with his low effort on 69 minutes. Roberts was replaced by Ben Anderson for the Rocks and Nasha went into the book as he pulled Nevill back.

Scott pulled out a wonderful save down to his right to keep Grant’s low volleyed effort from just outside the area. Ferdinand was offside on the rebound.

Ollie Lovell came off on 80 minutes for Bognor, then the referee pulled up injured with a strained calf so Bognor's public address announcer, Peter Kelly-Sullivan, had to take up the flag for linesman’s duty for the remainder of the game.

Brendan Matthew had a header diverted wide when he had the goal at his mercy in the 94th minute.

It was a nervy final moments for the Rocks with the visitors always a danger but they held on for the win.

Next up is the highly-anticipated game away to Jersey Bulls – and over 200 Bognor fans are expected to make the trip to the island on Saturday.

Rangers looked in danger of leaving Fir Park frustrated on Saturday night after a performance in which their attacking intent was not always matched by clinical finishing. In his first sit-down interview in five months, Berrada tackled topics ranging from the relationship between the Glazers and Ineos, the imminent departure of youngster JJ Gabriel, the decision not to sign a left back in the summer, as well as the decision to push ahead for a fresh stadium despite supporter backlash on matchdays.

The United chief has been at the centre of furious protests and anti-ownership chanting at matches this season, alongside Director of Football Jason Wilcox, and he accepted that criticism of United's leadership has, mostly, been fair.

In an interview that aired shortly after new head coach Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time, Berrada was pressed on how much accountability falls at his door with United heading to Anfield this weekend 18th in the Premier League table.

'I think if you think about the fact we've had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven't achieved the stability that we wanted, that's for sure,' Berrada told Sky Sports.

'When it doesn't work out with the coach or the manager, we are all responsible. Myself, the football leadership, everyone who is involved around the coach and the staff and the players. We have to continue improving and getting better.

Manchester United's CEO Omar Berrada finally fronted up in an interview with Sky Sports.

Michael Carrick's sacking was yet another managerial change at United, with the hierarchy under massive scrutiny and Mauricio Pochettino now in the hotseat.

'There are different circumstances why it didn't work out with Erik [ten Hag], and Ruben [Amorim], and now Michael [Carrick], and we are always learning and, as I mentioned, trying to improve and understand what has failed.

'The challenge is we're trying to find the right manager for the squad that we have with a specific set of skills in that moment to make them perform at their best level.

Recent findings suggest that 'It's true, we have to accept the criticism that we haven't been able to achieve that stability with one coach and our aim is to do that as soon as possible. Of course, we hope now that Mauricio coming in will give us that stability that I think we all need.'.

Berrada's links to Manchester City, where he worked prior to joining United, were brought up, not least given he worked at the club during the period that City have had charges brought against them.

'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted.

But at his fresh home there are problems aplenty, not least having got another managerial appointment wrong, sacking Carrick less than six months after handing him a two-year deal, and so it was put to Berrada: is the club actually progressing?

'It's not good enough, not acceptable and that's why we've made the change that we made so that we can move forward,' he concluded.

(L-R) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Berrada and Jason Wilcox have drawn plenty of ire from Man United fans.

'But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth, to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. It's not always been that.

Industry observers note that 'Last year we finished third, we were happy with the squad, we were happy with the way we were going. And now, a few months later, we are not where we need to be. Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

According to recent reports, carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and swiftly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 22:35, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 01:26.

Fulham goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with an Achilles injury.

The Frenchman sustained the injury in a behind-closed-doors game against West Ham United during the international break.

Revealing the extent of the injury, Alvaro Arbeloa told reporters on Friday: "Unfortunately, Lecomte injured his Achilles tendon against West Ham, so he will be out for the rest of the season.

“We are sorry for him because he is very key and it was very sad.”.

Lecomte has not played in the Premier League this season, but he featured in three of Fulham’s EFL Cup games, including a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace last month.

As a result of Lecomte’s injury, Alex Borto and Dino Kaiser will be the backup options for the club’s undisputed first-choice goalkeeper Bernd Leno.

Arbeloa also revealed Emile Smith Rowe is unlikely to be fit for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off against Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium.

“Smith Rowe has some pain in his hip, so I think he won't be available for tomorrow.

“I think it’s nothing serious - some pain and discomfort, so we will see next week, but it doesn't look really serious.”.

The news of Smith Rowe's physical glitch represents the latest setback in what is proving to be a difficult campaign for the Arsenal academy product.

The 28-year-old made 37 Premier League appearances in Marco Silva's final season in charge, but he has featured in just four league games under Arbeloa due to injury and selection decisions.

In more positive news, Arbeloa explained that Tom Cairney could be in contention to return to the squad after missing the draw against Newcastle United before the international window.

If available, Cairney could have a role to play off the bench as Fulham look to end their woeful run of form against Manchester City.

The Cottagers have lost each of their last 17 Premier League games against the Citizens since they played out a 2-2 draw at Craven Cottage in September 2011.

Meanwhile, their last head-to-head victory took place in April 2009 when Clinton Dempsey netted a brace in a 3-1 win at the Etihad Stadium.

Yunus Musah has insisted that AC Milan must believe in the Scudetto, while also assessing his start to the campaign under Ruben Amorim.

Going into the summer, an uncertain fate awaited Musah. Massimiliano Allegri did not see him as a part of the plans for 2025-26 and so he was loaned to Atalanta, where he had a mixed year and ultimately returned as they did not use their option to buy him.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that many sources presumed that it would be a return in passing and that a fresh destination would be found, but Amorim had other intends. The new coach clearly saw something in the USA international, and he has become a regular starter regardless of the system used.

In a recent development, such is his importance, there is even talk of a renewal being discussed. Musah was interviewed by SportMediaset and it was published two days before the Serie A campaign resumes with a home game against Frosinone. His comments were transcribed by MilanNews.

Do you feel like a ‘wild card’ for Milan?

In a recent development, “A little less so this year because I haven’t changed positions as much, even though I can do that. I’ve been able to play in midfield and improve in that area.”.

“I think he watched my old games, because he already knew what he expected from me and what he could ask of me. He did his homework, he watched everything, and he already knew what and how he could use me.”.

We’ve never seen you play left-back at Milan like you did in Genoa: how did this idea come about?

It has been revealed that “I don’t know (laughs). This question is for the coach. Bartesaghi and Estupinan are very good, but that day he wanted a right-footed player on the left.”.

If it were up to you, where do you want to play most?

“I think playing in midfield. Not fixed, though, being able to go anywhere so I can get the ball, get deep, without being fixed.”.

Do you think Milan is improving? Is the Scudetto possible?

It has been revealed that “It’s possible. We train every day for it. We all have the dream and ambition of winning it, and we’ll do everything we can to get there.”.

Can you tell us what you remember about your time in the States?

What do you remember about America?

According to recent reports, “Playing for the United States helped me gain this sense of belonging. Until I was 17, I only had a passport, but now I feel part of the culture.”.

It has been revealed that “I can go there. I know the restaurants, the chains, the people from different states, the geography. I understand American people so much now.

“I have many passports, I lived and grew up in many countries, like here in Italy, in England, so I feel a bit of everything.”.

Have you ever returned to see your childhood homes?

Recent findings suggest that “Yes, in 2021 I returned to Newly introduced York. I saw the house where I lived that year. The Bronx. It was beautiful to see it. There was a piece missing from my memory, and it was nice to be able to connect it.”.

Is it true you have a cat named Bronx?

It has been revealed that “Yes. I left him with the neighbours in Valencia because I couldn’t take him to Milan.”.

Your family moved from America to Italy….

“My family was already in Italy, and my mother had to go back and forth to America.”.

What was your childhood like in Castelfranco Veneto?

It has been revealed that “Beautiful. It’s a place where my parents weren’t afraid to let me play all day outside in the parking lot near the apartment building.”.

Is it true that your parents’ years of financial sacrifice were years of financial hardship?

In a recent development, “Of course. Obviously, when I grew up, we weren’t rich, we didn’t have much money, but from the time I left home, even when I was little, my parents never let me go without anything. I hope I’m their pride, because they are mine.”.

According to recent reports, you have also played for Arsenal and Valencia. What were the transitions like?

“Playing for Arsenal was a great privilege, because I arrived from Italy at 9 years old, played with a small team, and immediately joined Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that “I was ready to move to the first team when I was 16, and Valencia had a strategy for me. I spent four wonderful years in Spain; it’s a city that will always remain in my heart.”.

What’s the atmosphere like in the dressing room?

“Last year I watched them a lot; they were a very solid team and difficult to beat. Amorim brought a very positive vibe, we understand each other. He understands the player very well and vice versa.

“It helps when he understands what the players need; he’s good at that, and the players in the team are pretty calm.”.

Is he someone who gets angry when necessary?

“Yes. After Ferencvaros he was very angry, like everyone else.”.

What ties do you have to Africa?

“My wife is from Zanzibar, my family is Ghanaian. So it’s nice to travel to our home countries in the summer.”.

Middlesbrough head coach Kim Hellberg hailed forward David Strelec after the forward notched in a 2-0 win over Bristol City.

Adilson Malanda opened the scoring at the Riverside before Strelec made sure of victory with his first goal since May.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He was leading the line ahead of free-scoring Will Lankshear, who was on the bench after missing two games with a hamstring injury.

Hellberg noted: “It was brilliant; breaking down a team we hadn’t beaten in nine games and a team which had lost only one of their last seven away games, I am happy.

“Breaking down the low block and scoring from a set-piece and from David makes me overall happy, with a clean sheet too.

“It was a massive moment for David. He has been very good since coming back, he’s shown how good he is in these two games. That goal was a beautiful team goal and he is a top player – you could see how happy he was for it.

“He is a brilliant human being, it’s easy for me to back him. I can see what he does every day. It is about having more quality players being ready to play.

“For Will we wanted to get him on, it’s notable for him to play and have that feeling. Everyone knows how good he is, I am happy to have him back.”.

Under-pressure Bristol City boss Michael Skubala was left frustrated at the way his side conceded the first goal, when Malanda was left unmarked in the area to head in a corner.

Once Strelec had added the second, City were on track to lose a third game in a row – meaning they have won just one of their last eight matches.

According to recent reports, skubala said: “This was a disappointing afternoon. We tried to nullify all their strengths so to concede from a set-piece when we did made for a difficult start, and the second goal killed us.

Recent findings suggest that “And when you assess our finishing, it hurt us. We hit the post three times, and if we get one of those it would be a different end to the game.

“It is very difficult to take because if that first goal doesn’t happen then it is a different game.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Barney Corkhill | 20 Nov 2026 23:32.

It has been revealed that liverpool have won more major trophies than Manchester United, leading the Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies count 69-68 on every senior competitive honour as of November 20, 2026.

With a margin that small, the answer depends on what you count, because leaving out the one-off 1986 Football League Super Cup puts the clubs level, while leaving out the Community Shield gives the Reds a clear lead.

Neither club has lifted a trophy since Liverpool's 2024-25 Premier League title, which nudged the Anfield outfit back ahead of their eternal rivals.

Liverpool and Manchester United share the record for English league titles with 20 each, after the Merseysiders' 2024-25 Premier League win matched the total the Red Devils reached in 2012-13.

United are stronger in the FA Cup, with 13 wins to Liverpool's eight, and in the Community Shield, which they have won or shared 21 times against 16 for the Anfield club.

Liverpool hold the record of 10 League Cups, four more than their rivals, and they are the only one of the pair to have won the Football League Super Cup, which was played only once.

The gap opens up in Europe, where six European Cups, three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups give the Reds 13 continental trophies to United's six.

Liverpool have more trophies than Manchester United on the fullest count, one ahead, and they also lead when Community Shields are left out.

United only draw level if the 1986 Football League Super Cup is removed or shared Community Shields are discounted, and they only go ahead on a count limited to the league, FA Cup and League Cup, which they lead 39-38.

That makes the Reds the more decorated club, since they lead or are level on every method that includes European competition, and the only count that favours the Old Trafford side ignores continental silverware altogether.

United's honours board leaves out the Super Cup and so indicates the rivals level, which is a fair reading, but even on that basis the Red Devils still need one more trophy to go ahead.

Opinion is split on whether the Community Shield should count as a genuine trophy, and the FA itself treats it as a friendly for disciplinary purposes, so bookings in it do not carry over into other domestic games.

The fixture has only been contested between the league champions and the FA Cup winners since 1974, and before that it was an invitational match.

Seven of United's Community Shields and three of Liverpool's came before that change, which strengthens the case for leaving the trophy out.

The Anfield club's own honours page lists 52 major men's honours, a figure that excludes both the Community Shield and the Football League Super Cup, and the Community Shield never appeared on the honours board at their old Melwood training ground either.

Counting the Football League Super Cup but not the Community Shield gives the Reds a 53-47 lead, a six-trophy cushion over the Red Devils.

The Football League Super Cup was set up after the Heysel Stadium disaster in May 1985 and the European ban on English clubs that followed, as a replacement competition for the six sides who would have played on the continent in 1985-86.

Liverpool beat Everton in a two-legged final held back until September 1986, winning 3-1 at Anfield and 4-1 at Goodison Park for a 7-2 aggregate victory.

The tournament was never played again, which is why some honours boards ignore it, and counting it or not decides whether the Merseysiders lead or the clubs are level.

A drawn Community Shield used to be shared, and Liverpool's list includes five shared editions (1964, 1965, 1977, 1986 and 1990), while United shared four (1965, 1967, 1977 and 1990).

The years 1965, 1977 and 1990 appear on both lists, and removing every shared Community Shield leaves both clubs on 64, another count where Man United can claim a tie but not a lead.

Manchester United have their strongest case at home, with 60 domestic honours to Liverpool's 55 when Community Shields and the Football League Super Cup are counted.

In the three main domestic competitions, the league, FA Cup and League Cup, the Red Devils lead 39-38 thanks to five more FA Cup wins.

Cup finals between the pair have been split evenly, as United won the 1977 FA Cup final 2-1 and the 1996 final 1-0, while the Reds won the League Cup finals of 1983 and 2003.

The 1983 final went to extra time, with Alan Kennedy and Ronnie Whelan cancelling out Norman Whiteside's opener for a 2-1 win, and Steven Gerrard and Michael Owen scored in the 2-0 win in Cardiff 20 years later.

According to recent reports, for every result between the two clubs rather than just the silverware, our Man Utd vs. Liverpool head-to-head record covers each meeting.

Liverpool's six European Cups are more than any other British team has won and double United's three, and that record is what separates the clubs.

The Reds add three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups, while United's six European trophies are completed by a Europa League, a Cup Winners' Cup and one UEFA Super Cup.

United edge the world honours 2-1, having won the 1999 Intercontinental Cup and the 2008 Club World Cup, while the Merseysiders won the Club World Cup in 2019.

For the stories behind several of those European nights, including the 2005 final in Istanbul, our rundown of Liverpool's 10 greatest comebacks goes back through the club's most dramatic recoveries.

Manchester United's modern haul was built under Sir Alex Ferguson, who won 38 trophies in 26 years in charge between 1986 and 2013, including 13 league titles, five FA Cups and two Champions League titles.

The teams behind that run feature heavily in our ranking of Manchester United's 10 greatest ever teams, which sets the Ferguson sides against the club's earlier eras.

The latest swings came in 2023-24, when Liverpool's League Cup win put them one ahead on the full count before the Red Devils beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final to draw level again.

The Reds' 2024-25 Premier League title then put them one clear, while on the count that ignores the Super Cup the same sequence went from a tie to a United lead and back to the current tie.

Liverpool and Manchester United are both in the 2026-27 Champions League league phase, so Europe offers the biggest single swing, alongside the FA Cup, the League Cup and the next Community Shield.

One trophy for United without a reply from Anfield would level the full count, while any Liverpool success would stretch the gap to two.

Liverpool appear to have a better chance of adding to their haul in the 2026-27 campaign, with Man United out of the League Cup and having seen any faint hopes of a title challenge evaporate amidst their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

The Old Trafford side are now led by Mauricio Pochettino, who became head coach in November 2026 after Michael Carrick was sacked.

To see what the newly introduced head coach brings, our breakdown of Pochettino's record against every Premier League club shows how his past teams have fared against each top-flight side.

For a view of current strength rather than history, our ranking of the best football teams in the world shows where Liverpool sit among Europe's elite.

Huddersfield Town head coach Martin Drury lamented the absence of his side’s “usual spark” after their 1-0 defeat to Leicester City.

The Terriers suffered just their second League One defeat of the season against the Foxes, who struck early in the second half through Louis Page.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Drury did not feel Huddersfield deserved to lose, but also conceded they did not do enough to claim three points.

Industry observers note that he noted: “I didn’t think we did enough to win the game but I don’t think we deserved to lose the game. At the top end of the pitch, we didn’t have the usual spark about us.

Recent findings suggest that “The goal we concede is beyond disappointing. It’s not a goal that’s well worked and has cut us open. It’s a long ball that we need to deal with better.

It has been revealed that “I’m not sure you’ll see a softer goal across the country. We could have created far more chances. We didn’t execute well enough.”.

Regarding their approach to tackling Leicester, Drury added: “We didn’t over respect them but realised they are the highest in the league for having the ball. We wanted to make sure that didn’t lead to chances.

Sources indicate that “There are things to learn and grow from, like our crossing into the box. You have to make things happen and I didn’t feel here we made it happen. We just lacked that little bit of quality in the final third.”.

It was a vital win for Leicester and one that eased the pressure on boss Russell Martin, who basked in the celebrations with fans following the full-time whistle.

He said: “It was a bit of relief for me really, because I’ve not done that this season. The fans were amazing here when we needed them. The last 15 minutes they were brilliant and I’m really grateful for that. Hopefully they can feel what we are trying to build.

It has been revealed that “My son has been telling me that he’s been desperate for a fist pump! But it was just a relief. And I’m so proud of the players.

Sources indicate that “There are good teams at the top. The league will start taking shape over the next five or six games.

Sources indicate that “But it’s a big win for us – for us to show our growth and improvement more than anything. And then whatever message it sends to everyone else will be that message.”.

York City manager Scott Lindsey “took encouragement” from his side’s goalless draw with Walsall.

The Minstermen could not make a breakthrough against the Saddlers, who sit just one point behind the North Yorkshire outfit in the League Two table.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It is not often York are kept at bay in the final third, but Lindsey did not read the riot act.

Industry observers note that he said: “It was a really good game and as good as a 0-0 draw can be. We maybe deserved a bit more than a point, but there weren’t too many chances in the game.

“We had goalscorers all over the pitch by the end of the match and it’s not like us not to score, but we tried as hard as we could and I think the players carried out the game blueprint really well on the ball.

“Alex (Hunt) had a massive chance in the first half, but there weren’t too many chances in the game and you have to give the opposition credit as well.

“I am still taking encouragement from the performance, as I believe whoever finishes above Walsall this season will be promoted and I’m also delighted with the way we defended.

“That’s our third clean sheet in a row (excluding the Jersey Mike’s Trophy) and we’ve put a lot of work into improving that side of our game.”.

Walsall boss Lee Grant applauded his 10-man team’s “great character” after they became the first league opponent to keep a clean sheet at York since Solihull Moors in September 2025.

The Saddlers held out for a 0-0 draw despite losing Courtney Clarke to injury in the 81st minute, having made all their permitted substitutions.

Grant stated: “Going down to 10 men for the last 15 minutes, I’m proud of the great character we showed and it’s nice to be able to not concede a goal despite those circumstances at a place where so many teams have found that hard.

“There’s a reason why they have the ball more than anybody else in this division and score lots of goals and that’s because they have good technical players and are well coached.

“But, through the course of a season, there are so many parts of your game that you have to be able to demonstrate to continue performing well and I think we are showing all of those sides and I thought both teams defended their goals well.

“We maybe had enough of the game to warrant better chances than we created at times but, in the first half especially, we showed how we can control matches.”.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.

Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.

The Dutchman has helped the Merseyside club win numerous pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-19 Champions League.

However, it is unclear how much longer he will play a part in Liverpool's quest for trophies, with his current contract set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk recently commented on his situation while on international duty, insisting that he is "not in any panic" over his Anfield future.

The centre-back has reiterated his relaxed outlook in an interview with Sky Sports, in which he conceded he has "no idea" whether he will sign a latest Liverpool deal.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk remarked.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone indicates that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game.

"Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a massive part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

Recent findings suggest that "If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.".

At the age of 35, Van Dijk remains an integral part of the Liverpool squad, demonstrated by the fact he has played every minute of the club's 10 Premier League matches this term.

Van Dijk is now preparing to make his 350th Premier League appearance in Sunday's highly anticipated clash against rivals Manchester United.

The Netherlands international has made 282 of his 349 top-flight appearances in a Liverpool shirt after featuring in 67 Premier League matches for Southampton.

Van Dijk will hope to mark his milestone outing with a victory, although he has had to settle for seven wins in his previous 18 Premier League matches against Man United (D5, L6).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:01 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:06 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has warned that Manchester United cannot be stuck in the past as he begins the job of dragging the biggest club in English football out of the Premier League relegation zone.
  • Pochettino faces a huge first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, and he is determined to make a fresh start at United uninhibited by the history of the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 04:01 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:06 EST, 20 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino has warned that Manchester United cannot be stuck in the past as he begins the job of dragging the biggest club in English football out of the Premier League relegation zone.

Pochettino faces a huge first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, and he is determined to make a fresh start at United uninhibited by the history of the club.

‘We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy, in the way that we love to work. I think our job is to adapt and to go ahead a little bit,’ he said at Carrington.

Sources indicate that ‘The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear. It's an historic club with years being one of the best clubs in the world. It's difficult to find another club the size of Manchester United. It needs to be in a different place than we are now, no?

‘But I don't think too much in the past. If we want to create something different and positive, and the people feel proud about that, it's about building our own way here. Thinking on what happened yesterday is not going to help. You cannot be stuck in the past.’.

Pochettino’s appointment at United has been a whirlwind after the Argentine oversaw his final two games in charge of the US national team before flying through the night to start work on Wednesday.

Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time as Man United boss on Friday.

‘I think it's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool, and now our focus is 100 per cent on Liverpool,’ he added.

‘My first target is to sleep, but I cannot sleep – only three or four hours per day – but I think the target is to know the people, the staff, all the people here in the club, and of course the players and try from the beginning to have a positive impact.’.

In a recent development, pochettino admits he has missed being involved in day-to-day coaching at club level, saying: ‘Of course, we missed it a lot. We are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass, we need to smell the grass and to help the players to improve every day.

‘It's true that it's a different job when you are in the national team, but I think we are much better coaches now.’.

The 54-year-old told United that he wants to be involved in the all the key decision-making and transfers despite only being named as the club’s head coach.

Pochettino demanded more control during his five years in charge of Tottenham, and the difference between manager and head coach has also been a bone of contention at United in recent years.

Manchester United travel to rivals Liverpool on Sunday searching for their first league win since August.

Ruben Amorim was sacked after taking on the United hierarchy over his job title, while Erik ten Hag refused to give up his power to veto transfers.

Pochettino noted: ‘I know that being a head coach, I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday and I'm going to pick the starting 11.

‘I'm going to make the changes and of course that, in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen in the squad. That is (why) in the end, Manchester United is a football club, no?

Sources indicate that ‘During all my (career), when I started at Espanyol, head coach, coach, manager. In the end, it's not changing too much because I think the way that we work is indifferent to the title description.

‘If you are manager it’s not necessarily that you have all the decisions. Maybe you are a coach and have more power in the decision.’.

Pochettino revealed that he met most of the players individually at Carrington on Thursday, including captain Bruno Fernandes who cut a frustrated figure towards the end of Michael Carrick’s time in charge.

Pochettino confirmed that out-of-form Bruno Fernandes will remain as United captain.

‘Bruno is our captain and I think he's a very crucial player, but all the players need to feel that they are important from the top to the bottom,’ said Pochettino.

‘Yesterday we spent three hours chatting in an individual way in my office with all the players.’.

Concerns have been raised over the players’ fitness and attitude under Carrick this season, with the statistics suggesting that United have not been running enough.

‘That's a good question, no?,’ said Pochettino. ‘It’s a debate that I don't like to go into because I think we cannot talk about things without context, and data is about context. I think it's very dangerous to talk. We are here not to denounce things, we are here to build something.’.

Pochettino later shared a message on Instagram thanking supporters for their 'warm welcome' and declared the Red Devils 'cannot afford to waste a moment'.

'An intense first few days. Thank you to everyone for a warm welcome,' the Argentine wrote.

'We cannot afford to waste a moment. All our energy and attention is focused on preparing for Sunday.

'We can say many things, but what matters is the work we do and what we show on the pitch.'.

Alex Bruce was “immensely proud” of his Rotherham United players after their goalless draw with Grimsby Town.

That pride, however, was mixed with anguish over certain refereeing decisions as the sides shared the points at Blundell Park.

Both goalkeepers made some crucial saves and the woodwork came to the Millers’ rescue in the first half as they picked up just their fifth away point of the campaign.

He remarked: “I was immensely proud of the team, proud of everyone involved, to be honest. Seeing the numbers we had behind the goal from up in the stands, and the connection between the players and supporters after a fighting display, made me proud.

“If we are going to start winning games and climbing that table, then we do need to first show the fight and the spirit that we indicated today.

“I have to be careful [speaking about officiating] because I keep getting in trouble. I’ll let people make their own judgement but I’ve seen Paul Mullin head in a goal without even making contact with their goalkeeper.

“The contact comes after he has made the header, so that is a clear goal for us that should stand.

“I get a bit of stick for showing my grievances towards officials and decisions made, but I don’t want to have to point these things out, so I will let those who have watched make their own minds up.”.

Grimsby boss David Artell, meanwhile, said: “I thought it was a competitive game, an entertaining one for a 0-0.

“Both teams could have easily come away with the win, but without speaking for Alex, he is probably a bit happier than we are with the result.

“We stay on an unbeaten run, but we don’t sugarcoat things because my job is to win, and we didn’t do quite enough today.

“There are mitigating factors, the number of injuries we have being one, but I always want to focus on the team I have out there.

“Against the ball, I thought we were very good against a tough team, a team that were in League One last season.

“They (Rotherham) are very competitive physically, with how many duels they win, but our lads stuck at it, and that’s how we got the clean sheet, without quite having the quality or right decisions in the final third to win.”.

Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3035 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems. Although in-plane topological vortex nanostructures arising from twisting-induced lateral strain modulation have been linked to periodic moiré patterns in freestanding perovskite layers1,2,3 and 2D bilayers4, their coupling to the interfacial dislocation network in twisted layers remains unresolved. Here we demonstrate that twisted freestanding SrTiO3 (STO) layers undergo interfacial reconstruction into a network of screw dislocations, accompanied by the emergence of in-plane topological vortices. Unlike in previous reports, these vortices are associated with the dislocation network rather than with geometric moiré patterns. Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) reveals a beam deflection texture in registry with the interfacial dislocation network. A machine learning interatomic potential, trained on first-principles calculations, together with phase-field modelling, confirms that competing strains within the dislocation network stabilize polar vortex–antivortex pairs; first-principles calculations further reveal the emergence of an electronic superlattice with a well-defined periodicity. Our results establish twist-controlled dislocation networks as a fresh and versatile route to designing local polar and electronic structures in oxide materials.

It has been revealed that a,b, The reconstructed 5° twisted interface maximizes Ti coordination in b compared with the rigid structure in a. This reconstruction favours fully coordinated Ti sites (CN = 6, pink and beige) by minimizing undercoordinated Ti regions (CN = 5, yellow and green). This induces a dislocation (shaded grey region) between the two undercoordinated stackings. The insets on the right depict atomic positions across the interface for a central unit cell, illustrating the coordination environment.

Unit-cell averaged εxx, εyy and εxy (from left to right) using the described nearest-neighbour scheme for the TiO2-terminated and SrO-terminated layers (from top to bottom, respectively).

a, MLIP-DFT relaxed atomic positions at a 5° twist showing Ti atoms in the top (light) and bottom (dark) interfacial layers, demonstrating the orthogonal screw dislocation network, with a magnified view on the right. b, Twist-angle dependence of the interface energy (blue) together with the computed and analytical dislocation lengths (orange). The background colour denotes the transition from well-defined dislocations to their absence. c–f, Dislocation lengths are measured using the interlayer distance as a signature. The analytical prediction given by d = (a/2)/sin(θ/2) (orange line) matches the measured dislocation lengths.

Phase-field model predicted polarization components Px, Py and Pz in blue, green and black, respectively, plotted as a function of the out-of-plane coordinate z in the 5° twisted bicrystal sampled at different positions (denoted by shapes). Werder Bremen vs Hamburger SV - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 04:57.
  • Werder Bremen will be battling to keep their unlikely European dream alive on Sunday, when they welcome Hamburger SV to the Weserstadion for a Bundesliga Nordderby.
  • Die Werderaner are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while HSV are keen to pick up where they left off prior to the international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 04:57.

Werder Bremen will be battling to keep their unlikely European dream alive on Sunday, when they welcome Hamburger SV to the Weserstadion for a Bundesliga Nordderby.

Die Werderaner are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while HSV are keen to pick up where they left off prior to the international break.

Daniel Thioune guided Werder to safety last term after taking the helm in early February, though his sights are set much higher this time around with his team sat in a strong position upon the league's return.

Nine matches into the campaign, Die Werderaner are sixth in the Bundesliga table, where their tally of 15 points has them two clear of seventh-placed Elversberg and just three shy of RB Leipzig in fourth.

Securing European football of any variety would be a major accomplishment for Thioune, who is currently in his first top-flight role as manager, not to mention that the club last appeared on the continental stage back in the 2010-11 Champions League group stage.

However, Werder signed off for the international break with a 1-0 defeat at Stuttgart on November 7, their second loss in three matches after a 3-2 beating by Borussia Dortmund in the DFB-Pokal in late October.

In fairness to the Green-Whites, they fought back from 2-0 down against BVB thanks to a brace from Niclas Fullkrug, only to lose out to a stoppage-time free kick by Marcel Sabitzer.

Additionally, a 2-0 victory over Hoffenheim between those defeats saw the hosts maintain their unbeaten streak on home turf this season, where they will hope to record a fourth win in five outings on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Merlin Polzin's Hamburger endured a dire start to the season, conceding 12 goals without reply in their first three Bundesliga games before firing back with a run of three consecutive triumphs.

It would be fair to say that HSV's term has been defined by streaks so far, alternating between trios of defeats and wins across all competitions, and the club will be hoping to stabilise after the international break.

Polzin's side were held to a 1-1 draw by Croatia's Hajduk Split in a friendly on November 15, following up a 3-1 success against Borussia Monchengladbach that helped to distance the team from the relegation zone in the German top flight.

That victory has left Hamburger 11th in the Bundesliga table with 12 points to their name - a total that puts them level with Eintracht Frankfurt, Hoffenheim and Stuttgart up to eighth - as well as five points clear of 16th-placed Union Berlin.

Earning another win on Sunday would be keeping with HSV's pattern this term, but after seeing the visitors lose four of their five away league matches in 2026-27, fans would be forgiven for harbouring doubts.

Werder Bremen form (all competitions):.

Hamburger SV form (all competitions):.

Werder will be without strikers Keke Topp (ACL) and Salim Musah (thigh) once again as they recover from long-term injuries, though the doubts about Marco Grull's fitness after he missed training with a calf problem will be a major concern for the team.

If Grull is sidelined on Sunday, then expect to see Niclas Fullkrug supported up top by Eren Dinkci, Chuki and Justin Njinmah.

Jens Stage and Skelly Alvero are also unavailable due to respective thigh and calf injuries, while question marks remain about the readiness of fellow midfielder Senne Lynen, who has been ill over the past week, though Youri Regeer and Ludovit Reis should be on hand to form Thioune's double pivot.

Elsewhere, the versatile Mitchell Weiser is a doubt with a thigh problem and left-back Moussa N'Diaye is recovering from a groin injury, so Arthur and Olivier Deman look set to start at full-back.

As for Hamburger, they are missing centre-back Jordan Torunarigha, who has been dealing with a hip concern, but Mario Vuskovic is likely to return after getting over a minor back injury.

The visitors are lighter in midfield than ideal, with all three of Albert Sambi Lokonga (calf), Bilal Nadir (thigh) and Nicolai Remberg (ACL) sidelined, so Martin Adeline could join Miro Muheim in the centre of the park, while Albert Gronbaek operates in the number 10 role.

Centre-forward Yussuf Poulsen is also out with a calf injury, but Terem Moffi and Patson Daka will be ready to lead the line in a strike partnership on Sunday.

Werder Bremen possible starting lineup:.

Hein; Arthur, Friedl, Pieper, Deman; Regeer, Reis; Dinkci, Chuki, Njinmah; Fullkrug.

Hamburger SV possible starting lineup:.

Heuer; Capaldo, Omari, Bornauw; El Ouahdi, Adeline, Muheim, Moller Wolfe; Gronbaek; Moffi, Daka.

Werder have been exceptional on home turf this season, and they will be expecting to collect all three points once again, but the match is likely to be closer than otherwise if Grull remains sidelined.

By contrast, Hamburger have struggled on the road throughout 2026-27, and with four defeats in five away Bundesliga games so far, expect to see the visitors' overall pattern of results broken.
